Aatrox.name: Aatrox
Aatrox.title: the Darkin Blade
Aatrox.blurb: Once honored defenders of Shurima against the Void, Aatrox and his brethren would eventually become an even greater threat to Runeterra, and were defeated only by cunning mortal sorcery. But after centuries of imprisonment, Aatrox was the first to find...
Aatrox.Notes: Aatrox rewards landing his W chains for healing and tempo, and his E gap-close plus Q knockup let him force fights, but he's vulnerable to sustained kiting, disengage, and true damage/healing-reduction champions who punish his lack of range.

Ahri.name: Ahri
Ahri.title: the Nine-Tailed Fox
Ahri.blurb: Innately connected to the magic of the spirit realm, Ahri is a fox-like vastaya who can manipulate her prey's emotions and consume their essence—receiving flashes of their memory and insight from each soul she consumes. Once a powerful yet wayward...
Ahri.Notes: Ahri's Charm-into-Ultimate combo makes her one of the strongest pick champions in the game, and her R reset lets her chain kills, and her Spirit Rush gives her great disengage and roam potential, but she's vulnerable to burst assassins who can jump on her before she can react and untargetable/dash-heavy champions who can dodge her skillshots.

Akali.name: Akali
Akali.title: the Rogue Assassin
Akali.blurb: Abandoning the Kinkou Order and her title of the Fist of Shadow, Akali now strikes alone, ready to be the deadly weapon her people need. Though she holds onto all she learned from her master Shen, she has pledged to defend Ionia from its enemies, one...
Akali.Notes: Akali's stealth cloud (W) makes her hard to punish once she engages, but she's heavily reliant on landing her E to targets. True-damage/AoE-suppress champions or those with hard CC that ignores stealth can shut her down before she gets going.

Akshan.name: Akshan
Akshan.title: the Rogue Sentinel
Akshan.blurb: Raising an eyebrow in the face of danger, Akshan fights evil with dashing charisma, righteous vengeance, and a conspicuous lack of shirts. He is highly skilled in the art of stealth combat, able to evade the eyes of his enemies and reappear when they...
Akshan.Notes: Akshan punishes overextending champions with his passive (marking and executing recently-killed-ally killers) and can revive fallen teammates with his ultimate, but he has no hard escape or disengage tool, making him vulnerable to burst assassins and dive comps that can jump him down before he can kite or reposition.

Alistar.name: Alistar
Alistar.title: the Minotaur
Alistar.blurb: Always a mighty warrior with a fearsome reputation, Alistar seeks revenge for the death of his clan at the hands of the Noxian empire. Though he was enslaved and forced into the life of a gladiator, his unbreakable will was what kept him from truly...
Alistar.Notes: Alistar's Q-W combo lets him headbutt an enemy into his own knockup for a devastating all-in engage, and his ultimate makes him extremely hard to kill or peel off once committed, but he's very mana-hungry early and easily neutralized by hard CC (like Morgana's Black Shield) that stops his engage before it lands.

Ambessa.name: Ambessa
Ambessa.title: Matriarch of War
Ambessa.blurb: All who know the name Medarda respect and fear the family's leader, Ambessa. As a Noxian general, she embodies a deadly combination of ruthless strength and fearless resolve in battle. Her role as matriarch is no different, requiring great cunning to...
Ambessa.Notes: Ambessa is built around chaining dashes after every ability cast (her passive), letting her stick to a single target relentlessly in 1v1s, and her ultimate is a suppress-into-stun pick tool for isolating backline targets — but Riot explicitly designed her as a duelist with weaker teamfight presence, so she's most dangerous split-pushing or picking off stragglers rather than in messy 5v5s.

Amumu.name: Amumu
Amumu.title: the Sad Mummy
Amumu.blurb: Legend claims that Amumu is a lonely and melancholy soul from ancient Shurima, roaming the world in search of a friend. Doomed by an ancient curse to remain alone forever, his touch is death, his affection ruin. Those who claim to have seen him describe...
Amumu.Notes: Amumu's ultimate is one of the strongest AoE engage tools in the game, capable of locking down and deleting an entire team if positioned well, but he's extremely reliant on landing Bandage Toss to stick to a target beforehand, and he has almost no self-peel or escape if his engage whiffs or gets countered by tenacity/cleanse/spell shields.

Anivia.name: Anivia
Anivia.title: the Cryophoenix
Anivia.blurb: Anivia is a benevolent winged spirit who endures endless cycles of life, death, and rebirth to protect the Freljord. A demigod born of unforgiving ice and bitter winds, she wields those elemental powers to thwart any who dare disturb her homeland...
Anivia.Notes: Anivia's Wall and Frostbite give her unmatched zone control and waveclear, and her passive egg-revive makes her incredibly hard to permanently kill in lane, but she has zero mobility or escape once her Wall is on cooldown, making her extremely vulnerable to assassins and dive comps that can burst her egg before it hatches.

Annie.name: Annie
Annie.title: the Dark Child
Annie.blurb: Dangerous, yet disarmingly precocious, Annie is a child mage with immense pyromantic power. Even in the shadows of the mountains north of Noxus, she is a magical outlier. Her natural affinity for fire manifested early in life through unpredictable...
Annie.Notes: Annie's stun is tied to a passive stack system (every 4th ability cast auto-stuns), making her burst combo devastating and hard to play around once she has Tibbers up, but she has no mobility or escape tools, so she's extremely reliant on her stun/shield to survive dives and falls off if her passive stack is baited out prematurely.

Aphelios.name: Aphelios
Aphelios.title: the Weapon of the Faithful
Aphelios.blurb: Emerging from moonlight's shadow with weapons drawn, Aphelios kills the enemies of his faith in brooding silence—speaking only through the certainty of his aim, and the firing of each gun. Though fueled by a poison that renders him mute, he is guided by...
Aphelios.Notes: Aphelios has the steepest learning curve of any marksman due to his dual-weapon system (each with a unique effect requiring memorization and swapping via ammo depletion), but a well-played Aphelios has some of the best late-game teamfight damage output and range control in the game, especially with the right weapon combos (e.g., Gravitum root chains, Infernum AoE waves).

Ashe.name: Ashe
Ashe.title: the Frost Archer
Ashe.blurb: Iceborn warmother of the Avarosan tribe, Ashe commands the most populous horde in the north. Stoic, intelligent, and idealistic, yet uncomfortable with her role as leader, she taps into the ancestral magics of her lineage to wield a bow of True Ice...
Ashe.Notes: Ashe's passive slow on every auto-attack gives her strong kiting and lane control, and her ultimate is a long-range global pick/setup tool that can turn fights from across the map, but she has no mobility or escape tools and comparatively low raw damage output versus other ADCs, making her more of a utility/enabler carry than a hard scaling one.

AurelionSol.name: Aurelion Sol
AurelionSol.title: The Star Forger
AurelionSol.blurb: Aurelion Sol once graced the vast emptiness of the cosmos with celestial wonders of his own devising. Now, he is forced to wield his awesome power at the behest of a space-faring empire that tricked him into servitude. Desiring a return to his...
AurelionSol.Notes: Aurelion Sol's orbiting stars give him constant AoE waveclear and zone pressure, and his ultimate (a global-range flight that can be used offensively or to reposition across the map) gives him unmatched map presence for a mage, but he's mana-hungry and immobile outside of his Astral Flight's cooldown, and his damage relies on positioning stars correctly around enemies rather than simple point-and-click burst.

Aurora.name: Aurora
Aurora.title: the Witch Between Worlds
Aurora.blurb: From the moment she was born, Aurora navigated life with a unique ability to move between the spirit and material realms. Determined to learn more about the spirit realm's inhabitants, she left her home to further her research and happened upon a...
Aurora.Notes: Aurora's passive stacks a percent-health true damage burst on the third hit and grants healing/movement speed via exorcised spirits, while her E dash resets on takedowns for strong roam/kill potential, but her ultimate can be countered by dashes/blinks that let enemies escape the zone before the cage fully closes, and her medium range makes her vulnerable to hard-engage assassins in solo lanes.

Azir.name: Azir
Azir.title: the Emperor of the Sands
Azir.blurb: Azir was a mortal emperor of Shurima in a far distant age, a proud man who stood at the cusp of immortality. His hubris saw him betrayed and murdered at the moment of his greatest triumph, but now, millennia later, he has been reborn as an Ascended...
Azir.Notes: Azir's soldiers give him incredible zone control, waveclear, and peel through his shield-dash (E), and his ultimate can wall off entire areas or set up devastating knockback combos with teammates' CC, but he has very low base stats and no self-sustain, making him extremely vulnerable in the early game and reliant on his soldiers/positioning to survive until his mid-late game scaling kicks in.

Bard.name: Bard
Bard.title: the Wandering Caretaker
Bard.blurb: A traveler from beyond the stars, Bard is an agent of serendipity who fights to maintain a balance where life can endure the indifference of chaos. Many Runeterrans sing songs that ponder his extraordinary nature, yet they all agree that the cosmic...
Bard.Notes: Bard is one of the most map-roam-heavy supports in the game — his passive lets him collect meeps to empower his Q into a longer-range stun and gather health/mana from shrines, and his ultimate can freeze champions, monsters, and turrets in stasis anywhere on the map to swing objectives or fights, but he sacrifices consistent lane presence and peel for global impact, making him weaker if his roams don't pay off.

Belveth.name: Bel'Veth
Belveth.title: the Empress of the Void
Belveth.blurb: A nightmarish empress created from the raw material of an entire devoured city, Bel'Veth is the end of Runeterra itself... and the beginning of a monstrous reality of her own design. Driven by epochs of repurposed history, knowledge, and memories from...
Belveth.Notes: Bel'Veth's kit revolves around uncapped attack speed scaling and a true-form ultimate that massively boosts her stats, making her one of the strongest 1v9 scaling junglers in the game once she snowballs kills or objectives, but she has notably weak waveclear/early presence outside of skirmishes, and falls off hard against disengage/peel or hard CC that shuts down her all-in dueling before she can stack her passive.

Blitzcrank.name: Blitzcrank
Blitzcrank.title: the Great Steam Golem
Blitzcrank.blurb: Blitzcrank is an enormous, near-indestructible automaton from Zaun, originally built to dispose of hazardous waste. However, he found this primary purpose too restricting, and modified his own form to better serve the fragile people of the Sump...
Blitzcrank.Notes: Blitzcrank's Rocket Grab is one of the highest-impact single-target pick tools in the game, capable of instantly deleting an isolated squishy target and setting up his silence/knockup follow-up, but the entire kit revolves around landing that skillshot — if the hook misses, he has very little else to offer, and hard-CC-prevention tools (Morgana's Black Shield being the classic answer) shut him down completely.

Brand.name: Brand
Brand.title: the Burning Vengeance
Brand.blurb: Once a tribesman of the icy Freljord named Kegan Rodhe, the creature known as Brand is a lesson in the temptation of greater power. Seeking one of the legendary World Runes, Kegan betrayed his companions and seized it for himself—and, in an instant, the...
Brand.Notes: Brand's passive (Blaze) chains burning damage between enemies hit by his abilities, making his AoE burst devastating in teamfights and skirmishes, and his ultimate can spread massive damage across a whole grouped team, but he has zero mobility and no escape, making him extremely reliant on positioning/peel and easily punished by dive comps or assassins if caught out.

Braum.name: Braum
Braum.title: the Heart of the Freljord
Braum.blurb: Blessed with massive biceps and an even bigger heart, Braum is a beloved hero of the Freljord. Every mead hall north of Frostheld toasts his legendary strength, said to have felled a forest of oaks in a single night, and punched an entire mountain into...
Braum.Notes: Braum's passive (Concussive Blows) stacks a stun on enemies hit by him or his ADC's autos, giving the duo strong lane dominance and pick potential, and his shield (E) plus ultimate knockup make him one of the best peel/protect supports for a carry, but he has no self-mobility outside his passive-empowered dash and no sustain, making him vulnerable to poke/burst that whittles him and his carry down from range.

Briar.name: Briar
Briar.title: the Restrained Hunger
Briar.blurb: A failed experiment by the Black Rose, Briar's uncontrollable bloodlust required a special pillory to focus her frenzied mind. After years of confinement, this living weapon broke free from her restraints and unleashed herself into the world. Now she's...
Briar.Notes: Briar is fearless once she engages — her own kit self-locks her into aggression, so she wants peel or CC follow-up from her team to convert all-ins, and struggles if kited by ranged champions who can punish her lack of an escape.

Caitlyn.name: Caitlyn
Caitlyn.title: the Sheriff of Piltover
Caitlyn.blurb: Renowned as its finest peacekeeper, Caitlyn Kiramman is also Piltover's best shot at ridding the city of its elusive criminal elements. She is often paired with Vi, acting as a cool counterpoint to her partner's more impetuous nature. Even though she...
Caitlyn.Notes: Caitlyn has the longest auto-attack range of any marksman, letting her out-poke and out-trade almost every other ADC in lane, and her Q/E combo can set up long-range picks or execute low-health targets with her ultimate, but she has zero self-mobility and falls off in extended teamfights compared to hyper-carries, making her vulnerable to dive comps and assassins who can close the gap.

Camille.name: Camille
Camille.title: the Steel Shadow
Camille.blurb: Weaponized to operate outside the boundaries of the law, Camille is the Principal Intelligencer of Clan Ferros—an elegant and elite agent who ensures the Piltover machine and its Zaunite underbelly runs smoothly. Adaptable and precise, she views sloppy...
Camille.Notes: Camille's E lets her hookshot onto terrain for huge mobility/engage, and her ultimate isolates a single target by walling off their allies, making her one of the best dueling/pick champions for shutting down an enemy carry, but she has no AoE teamfight presence and her damage is heavily front-loaded into a single burst combo, so whiffing her E or ultimate leaves her without much follow-up.

Cassiopeia.name: Cassiopeia
Cassiopeia.title: the Serpent's Embrace
Cassiopeia.blurb: Cassiopeia is a deadly creature bent on manipulating others to her sinister will. Youngest and most beautiful daughter of the noble Du Couteau family of Noxus, she ventured deep into the crypts beneath Shurima in search of ancient power. There, she was...
Cassiopeia.Notes: Cassiopeia's ground-based poison zones (Q/E) create a persistent damage-over-time battlefield that punishes enemies for standing still or walking into her space, and her ultimate is a devastating team-wide stun if enemies are facing her, but she has zero mobility and must carefully manage facing/positioning to land her stun, making her extremely reliant on her team to protect her from dives.

Chogath.name: Cho'Gath
Chogath.title: the Terror of the Void
Chogath.blurb: From the moment Cho'Gath first emerged into the harsh light of Runeterra's sun, the beast was driven by the most pure and insatiable hunger. A perfect expression of the Void's desire to consume all life, Cho'Gath's complex biology quickly converts...
Chogath.Notes: Cho'Gath's passive (Carnivore) lets him permanently stack bonus health by landing abilities or killing units, making him one of the best scaling tanks in the game, and his ultimate (Feast) can execute low-health targets while granting another permanent stat stack on champion kills, but he has zero mobility, so he's vulnerable to being kited or dove before he stacks up, and his Rupture knockup can be dodged if telegraphed.

Corki.name: Corki
Corki.title: the Daring Bombardier
Corki.blurb: The yordle pilot Corki loves two things above all others: flying, and his glamorous mustache... though not necessarily in that order. After leaving Bandle City, he settled in Piltover and fell in love with the wondrous machines he found there. He...
Corki.Notes: Corki's kit is built around consistent mixed physical/true damage poke (his Q auto-resets and E rockets deal a percentage as true damage), letting him out-trade most mages in lane and shred through armor stacking, and his W (Valkyrie) gives him a short dash for repositioning or escape while also leaving a damaging fire trail behind him. He has no hard CC beyond a slow, so he still relies on setup or a peel-oriented ally to lock down targets before he can fully capitalize on his damage.

Darius.name: Darius
Darius.title: the Hand of Noxus
Darius.blurb: There is no greater symbol of Noxian might than Darius, the nation's most feared and battle-hardened commander. Rising from humble origins to become the Hand of Noxus, he cleaves through the empire's enemies—many of them Noxians themselves. Knowing that...
Darius.Notes: Darius's passive (Hemorrhage) stacks bleed damage on hit, and killing a bleeding target grants a large true-damage-empowered heal via his ultimate, letting him snowball extremely hard off a single successful trade or kill, but he has zero mobility and no escape, meaning he's very vulnerable to kiting, disengage, or champions who can outrange/outrun him until his own cooldowns and lane pressure fall off.

Diana.name: Diana
Diana.title: Scorn of the Moon
Diana.blurb: Bearing her crescent moonblade, Diana fights as a warrior of the Lunari—a faith all but quashed in the lands around Mount Targon. Clad in shimmering armor the color of winter snow at night, she is a living embodiment of the silver moon's power. Imbued...
Diana.Notes: Diana's Crescent Strike (Q) mark lets her E (Lunar Rush) reset onto the same target for free, chaining dashes to stick to a champion through an entire fight, and her Pale Cascade (W) shield plus passive attack-speed burst let her brawl surprisingly well in extended skirmishes for a caster; her ultimate pulls and slows everyone nearby to group them up for her cleave/AoE damage, but she has no hard CC, so she relies on landing Q or having allies lock a target down before she can guarantee her E resets and stick to a kill.

Draven.name: Draven
Draven.title: the Glorious Executioner
Draven.blurb: In Noxus, warriors known as Reckoners face one another in arenas where blood is spilled and strength tested—but none has ever been as celebrated as Draven. A former soldier, he found that the crowds uniquely appreciated his flair for the dramatic, and...
Draven.Notes: Draven's identity is entirely built around catching his spinning axes (Q) to keep the empowered bonus damage active and stack gold via his passive (Adoration) on kills/assists, making him one of the highest snowball-potential ADCs in the game when ahead, but he has no dash or blink, so he relies on his W's movement-speed boost to reposition and can fall off hard if he loses axe uptime or gets shut down before he can stack Adoration and gold-scale.

DrMundo.name: Dr. Mundo
DrMundo.title: the Madman of Zaun
DrMundo.blurb: Utterly mad, tragically homicidal, and horrifyingly purple, Dr. Mundo is what keeps many of Zaun's citizens indoors on particularly dark nights. Now a self-proclaimed physician, he was once a patient of Zaun's most infamous asylum. After "curing" the...
DrMundo.Notes: Dr. Mundo has no mana and his health-cost kit lets him fight and sustain almost indefinitely with enough max-health items, and his passive grants strong resistance to being fully locked down (he can move/act through most disables above a certain threshold), making him one of the hardest champions to permanently CC-lock or all-in kill; his damage scales heavily off max health rather than burst, so he's most dangerous late-game as a tank-bruiser hybrid, but he lacks any dash/blink and has almost no reliable CC of his own, making him rely on his team to peel or engage for him in teamfights.

Ekko.name: Ekko
Ekko.title: the Boy Who Shattered Time
Ekko.blurb: A prodigy from the rough streets of Zaun, Ekko is able to manipulate time to twist any situation to his advantage. He uses his own invention, the Z-Drive, to explore the branching possibilities of reality, crafting the perfect moment to seemingly...
Ekko.Notes: Ekko's W (Parallel Convergence) creates a delayed shockwave stun zone that rewards good prediction/setup, and his ultimate (Chronobreak) rewinds him to his position from a few seconds prior while dealing AoE damage and healing based on damage dealt to champions, making it an incredibly forgiving 'get out of jail free' escape that also punishes anyone who dove him; his E dash and passive slow give him strong dueling/kiting tools, but his stun is telegraphed and can be walked out of if the enemy reacts in time, so his all-in relies on covering the zone with other threats or catching someone out of position.

Elise.name: Elise
Elise.title: the Spider Queen
Elise.blurb: Elise is a deadly predator who dwells in a shuttered, lightless palace, deep within the oldest city of Noxus. Once mortal, she was the mistress of a powerful house, but the bite of a vile demigod transformed her into something beautiful, yet utterly...
Elise.Notes: Elise's human form (Cocoon stun + Volatile Spiderling nuke) excels at picking off isolated squishy targets from range, while her spider form (self-heal via Spider Swarm, Skitter gap-close, and Rappel escape/engage) makes her a strong dueling shapeshifter once she commits, but she has to constantly manage her form-swap cooldown and mana/health tradeoffs, and she falls off hard against tanky, sustain-heavy junglers who can outlast her burst or hard-CC her before she lands Cocoon.

Evelynn.name: Evelynn
Evelynn.title: Agony's Embrace
Evelynn.blurb: Within the dark seams of Runeterra, the demon Evelynn searches for her next victim. She lures in prey with the voluptuous façade of a human female, but once a person succumbs to her charms, Evelynn's true form is unleashed. She then subjects her victim...
Evelynn.Notes: Evelynn is stealthed and largely invisible to wards at level 6, making her a strong pick-oriented snowball jungler, but she falls off hard if she can't get ahead early since she has no reliable waveclear or teamfight presence outside of picks.

Ezreal.name: Ezreal
Ezreal.title: the Prodigal Explorer
Ezreal.blurb: A dashing adventurer, unknowingly gifted in the magical arts, Ezreal raids long-lost catacombs, tangles with ancient curses, and overcomes seemingly impossible odds with ease. His courage and bravado knowing no bounds, he prefers to improvise his way...
Ezreal.Notes: Ezreal is one of the few ADCs with zero crowd control in his kit, relying entirely on his Mystic Shot (Q) poke and Arcane Shift (E) blink to stay safe while chipping down opponents from range, and his ultimate (Trueshot Barrage) is a global-range poke/pick tool that can snipe low-health targets or secure objectives across the map, but his complete lack of CC means he offers little lockdown or peel for his team and relies entirely on positioning and his blink to survive dives.

Fiddlesticks.name: Fiddlesticks
Fiddlesticks.title: the Ancient Fear
Fiddlesticks.blurb: Something has awoken in Runeterra. Something ancient. Something terrible. The ageless horror known as Fiddlesticks stalks the edges of mortal society, drawn to areas thick with paranoia where it feeds upon terrorized victims. Wielding a jagged scythe...
Fiddlesticks.Notes: Fiddlesticks's ultimate (Crowstorm) is a short-range blink and channels repeated AoE damage, making him one of the strongest ambush/teamfight-swing junglers in the game when he can catch a group of enemies unaware, and his passive lets him camouflage in bushes/terrain to set up ganks or bait overextensions; his E (Reap) silence and Q (Terrify) fear give him strong lockdown to chain a kill once he's engaged, but outside of his ultimate he has no self-mobility, so if his ambush is spotted early or he's caught without Crowstorm up, he's very vulnerable.

Fiora.name: Fiora
Fiora.title: the Grand Duelist
Fiora.blurb: The most feared duelist in all Valoran, Fiora is as renowned for her brusque manner and cunning mind as she is for the speed of her bluesteel rapier. Born to House Laurent in the kingdom of Demacia, Fiora took control of the family from her father in...
Fiora.Notes: Fiora's passive (Duelist's Dance) marks four vital points on an enemy — hitting one heals her and grants attack speed, and her ultimate (Grand Challenge) reveals all four at once and buffs the healing/speed massively, making her one of the best pure 1v1 dueling champions in the game with proper execution; her W (Riposte) is a parry that blocks incoming damage/CC entirely and counter-damages the source, giving her a strong answer to burst or hard-engage all-ins, but she has no reliable AoE damage or CC, making her far weaker in messy teamfights than in isolated duels, and champions with true damage or percent-max-health damage that ignores her healing/parry timing can still punish her.

Fizz.name: Fizz
Fizz.title: the Tidal Trickster
Fizz.blurb: Fizz is an amphibious yordle, who dwells among the reefs surrounding Bilgewater. He often retrieves and returns the tithes cast into the sea by superstitious captains, but even the saltiest of sailors know better than to cross him—for many are the tales...
Fizz.Notes: Fizz's E (Playful/Trickster) lets him hop into the air and briefly become untargetable, dodging skillshots, turret shots, and even some hard CC entirely, then slam back down for bonus damage, making him one of the trickiest melee assassins to pin down in a duel; his ultimate (Chum the Waters) is a delayed fish-spear that knocks up and slows a target and nearby enemies when it lands, giving him solid teamfight/pick potential, but he's fairly squishy and mana-hungry early, and any suppression, hard point-and-click CC, or true damage that bypasses his untargetability window can shut down his combo before he escapes.

Galio.name: Galio
Galio.title: the Colossus
Galio.blurb: Outside the gleaming city of Demacia, the stone colossus Galio keeps vigilant watch. Built as a bulwark against enemy mages, he often stands motionless for decades until the presence of powerful magic stirs him to life. Once activated, Galio makes the...
Galio.Notes: Galio's ultimate (Hero's Entrance) lets him leap to a marked ally anywhere on the map and knock up/damage enemies on landing, making him one of the best long-range save/engage tools in the game and a premier roaming pick into heavy AP compositions thanks to his passive's bonus magic resist; his W (Shield of Durand) taunts nearby enemies after a brief delay, letting him lock down and protect a target simultaneously, but his kit is fairly telegraphed (both W and E require good read/positioning) and he lacks any hard engage against mobile champions who can simply walk or dash away before his slower setup abilities land.

Gangplank.name: Gangplank
Gangplank.title: the Saltwater Scourge
Gangplank.blurb: As unpredictable as he is brutal, the dethroned reaver king Gangplank is feared far and wide. Once, he ruled the port city of Bilgewater, and while his reign is over, there are those who believe this has only made him more dangerous. Gangplank would see...
Gangplank.Notes: Gangplank's passive (Trial by Fire) applies a stacking burn on-hit and his Q (Parrrley) executes low-health targets while refunding gold/cooldown on a kill, letting him snowball hard and scale into a monstrous split-push/poke threat with Death's Daughter (his cannon-barrage passive-item interaction) and his E's healing-cleanse; his ultimate (Cannon Barrage) is a massive global-range zone that damages and slows an entire area anywhere on the map, giving him some of the best siege/zone-denial and pick potential in the game, but he has zero self-mobility, making him vulnerable to gap-closing dive champions who can punish him before his Remove Scurvy (E) cleanse or Parrrley poke can stabilize the fight.

Garen.name: Garen
Garen.title: The Might of Demacia
Garen.blurb: A proud and noble warrior, Garen fights as one of the Dauntless Vanguard. He is popular among his fellows, and respected well enough by his enemies—not least as a scion of the prestigious Crownguard family, entrusted with defending Demacia and its...
Garen.Notes: Garen's Q (Decisive Strike) silences and grants a movement speed burst, letting him lock down and stick to spellcasters who rely on abilities to peel or fight back, and his passive (Perseverance) gives him strong out-of-combat healing that punishes poke-based lanes if they can't finish him off before he resets; his ultimate (Demacian Justice) is a true-damage execute that scales with the target's missing health, making him a real threat to squishies at any point in the game, but he has no dash, blink, or ranged tools, so kiting champions with sustained ranged pressure or high mobility can consistently outrun and whittle him down before he closes the distance.

Gnar.name: Gnar
Gnar.title: the Missing Link
Gnar.blurb: Gnar is a primeval yordle whose playful antics can erupt into a toddler's outrage in an instant, transforming him into a massive beast bent on destruction. Frozen in True Ice for millennia, the curious creature broke free and now hops about a changed...
Gnar.Notes: Gnar's passive Rage meter builds from dealing/taking damage and eventually forces a transformation into Mega Gnar, swapping him from a ranged poke/kiting kit (boomerang Q, hopping E) into a melee AoE-knockup bruiser (E becomes Wallop, which stuns if it pins the target against a wall or terrain), giving him a unique dual playstyle within a single champion; his mini-form hop (E) also lets him leap over walls for mobility or engage, but he has to manage his rage meter carefully since being caught in the wrong form (ranged when he needs burst, or melee when he needs to kite) can lose a fight, and he has fairly low base sustain outside of his kit's utility.

Gragas.name: Gragas
Gragas.title: the Rabble Rouser
Gragas.blurb: Equal parts jolly and imposing, Gragas is a massive, rowdy brewmaster who's always on the lookout for new ways to raise everyone's spirits. Hailing from parts unknown, he searches for ingredients among the unblemished wastes of the Freljord to help him...
Gragas.Notes: Gragas's E (Body Slam) is a self-dash that damages and slows on impact, doubling as both an engage and escape tool, and his passive/W (Drunken Rage) give him solid self-healing and a strong burst nuke that empowers his next ability, but the real centerpiece of his kit is his ultimate (Explosive Cask), a long-range barrel throw that knocks back and damages a wide area, making him one of the best pick/peel/engage tools in the game if aimed well; the knockback is a skillshot, though, so a well-timed dash or displacement-immunity can dodge or shrug off its impact.

Graves.name: Graves
Graves.title: the Outlaw
Graves.blurb: Malcolm Graves is a renowned mercenary, gambler, and thief—a wanted man in every city and empire he has visited. Even though he has an explosive temper, he possesses a strict sense of criminal honor, often enforced at the business end of his...
Graves.Notes: Graves's passive (New Destiny) gives his shotgun-style autos limited ammo that requires periodic reloading, and non-champion units hit by multiple bullets get knocked back, giving him strong jungle-camp control and kiting; his Q (End of the Line) is an explosive shell that detonates on hitting a champion or terrain, dealing bonus cone damage on impact; his W (Smoke Screen) throws a canister that blinds enemy vision outside its radius while slowing and damaging on initial impact, useful for disengaging, hiding an all-in, or denying an enemy's follow-up; and his E (Quickdraw) is a dash that reloads a shell and grants stacking bonus armor (extra stacks if dashed toward an enemy champion), with autos reducing its cooldown — and because the recoil from Collateral Damage knocks him backward, he can use it to hop over walls and escape after securing a kill. His ultimate (Collateral Damage) fires a long-range, high-damage shell that explodes into a cone on impact, making it one of the best execute/finisher tools among junglers. But his attack range is notably short for a marksman-style champion, and his effectiveness depends heavily on hitting skillshots and timing Quickdraw's reload window correctly, so long-range poke champions who can punish his short range before he closes distance give him the most trouble.

Gwen.name: Gwen
Gwen.title: The Hallowed Seamstress
Gwen.blurb: A former doll transformed and brought to life by magic, Gwen wields the very tools that once created her. She carries the weight of her maker's love with every step, taking nothing for granted. At her command is the Hallowed Mist, an ancient and...
Gwen.Notes: Gwen's passive (Thousand Cuts) deals bonus true damage scaling with the target's max health on every few hits, making her a strong duelist against tanks and bruisers alike, and her W (Hallowed Mist) creates a personal mist zone that reduces incoming damage from outside it while granting her bonus magic resist and move speed inside, giving her a strong defensive tool during extended trades; her E (Skip'n Slash) dash resets on hitting an enemy champion, letting her chain repositions in a fight, and her ultimate (Needlework) fires a volley of needles that slows on the each hit, but she has fairly low mobility outside of E cooldown and can be kited or poked down by ranged champions before she closes the gap.

Hecarim.name: Hecarim
Hecarim.title: the Shadow of War
Hecarim.blurb: Hecarim is a spectral fusion of man and beast, cursed to ride down the souls of the living for all eternity. When the Blessed Isles fell into shadow, this proud knight was obliterated by the destructive energies of the Ruination, along with all his...
Hecarim.Notes: Hecarim's E (Devastating Charge) builds bonus movement speed and damage the longer he runs before hitting a target, letting him barrel down a lane and knock up anyone in his path, while his passive and Q (Rampage) grant on-hit healing that scales with his bonus movement speed, making him a strong extended-fight duelist when he's built up speed; his ultimate (Onslaught of Shadows) grants a huge global movement-speed boost to him and nearby allies while summoning ghosts that fear enemies in a line, giving him one of the best teamfight-initiation and map-roaming tools among junglers, but he telegraphs his charge-up on E, so hard CC or displacement-immunity can interrupt his engage before it lands.

Heimerdinger.name: Heimerdinger
Heimerdinger.title: the Revered Inventor
Heimerdinger.blurb: The eccentric Professor Cecil B. Heimerdinger is one of the most innovative and esteemed inventors the world has ever known. As the longest serving member of the Council of Piltover, he saw the best and the worst of the city's unending desire for...
Heimerdinger.Notes: Heimerdinger's H-28G turrets (Q) provide relentless zone control and waveclear by auto-attacking anything that walks into range, letting him lock down large areas of the map or lane while sitting safely behind them, and his E (CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade) stuns if it lands directly on a target, giving him solid pick potential; his W (Hextech Micro-Rockets) is a cone of homing rockets that slow, reinforcing his zone-denial identity, but he has zero personal mobility and turrets take time to set up, making him extremely vulnerable if dove before his defenses are established or if caught without turret cover.

Hwei.name: Hwei
Hwei.title: the Visionary
Hwei.blurb: Hwei is a brooding painter who creates brilliant art in order to confront Ionia's criminals and comfort their victims. Beneath his melancholy roils a torn, emotional mind—haunted by both the vibrant visions of his imagination and the gruesome memories...
Hwei.Notes: Hwei's Q, W, and E each open a 'Subject' spellbook of three sub-spells rather than being single fixed abilities, giving him effectively nine base spells plus a passive and ultimate: Subject: Disaster (Q) holds his main damage spells, Subject: Serenity (W) holds utility spells like speed and shields for allies, and Subject: Torment (E) holds his crowd control spells — Grim Visage fears, Gaze of the Abyss roots/slows, and Crushing Maw pulls enemies together and slows them, functioning as his only multi-target CC.  His passive (Signature Spawn) detonates a burst of extra damage under a target after he lands two damage spells on them, rewarding chaining different Q spells together; and his ultimate (Spiraling Despair) marks the first enemy champion hit with an expanding zone that slows and damages nearby enemies. This gives him an unmatched toolkit for adapting to whatever a fight needs — pure poke, peel, CC, or wave clear — but every spell requires a two-part cast (choosing the Subject, then the specific spell), making him one of the highest-skill-ceiling, most mechanically demanding mages in the game, and he has no mobility of his own, so mobile assassins who can close the distance before he can react with the right tool remain his biggest threat.

Illaoi.name: Illaoi
Illaoi.title: the Kraken Priestess
Illaoi.blurb: Illaoi's powerful physique is dwarfed only by her indomitable faith. As the prophet of the Great Kraken, she uses a huge, golden idol to rip her foes' spirits from their bodies and shatter their perception of reality. All who challenge the “Truth Bearer...
Illaoi.Notes: Illaoi's E (Test of Spirit) pulls out an enemy's spirit and punishes them with damage/healing-debuff if they can't sever the tether by staying near it, and her Q (Tentacle Smash) summons tentacles from nearby corpses or spirits that slam an area for heavy damage, letting her carve out a devastating zone in extended fights; her ultimate (Leap of Faith) slams down and spawns tentacles from all corpses/spirits in the area, healing her based on how many enemies are hit, giving her some of the best sustained 1v1 and split-push potential in the game, but she has zero self-mobility and no hard CC, so mobile ranged champions can kite her endlessly and deny her tentacle setups before she stacks enough pressure to win.

Irelia.name: Irelia
Irelia.title: the Blade Dancer
Irelia.blurb: The Noxian occupation of Ionia produced many heroes, none more unlikely than young Irelia of Navori. Trained in the ancient dances of her province, she adapted her art for war, using the graceful and carefully practised movements to levitate a host of...
Irelia.Notes: Irelia's Q (Bladesurge) is a dash to an enemy that resets its cooldown on a champion takedown or minion/monster kill near death, letting her chain resets across a wave or fight for huge mobility and burst; her E (Flawless Duet) sends out two blades that root if an enemy is caught between them, and her ultimate (Vanguard's Edge) launches multiple blades that stun anyone trapped between two, but both of these CC tools require precise positioning of two separate projectiles, making them highly skill-dependent and easy to avoid against an aware or mobile opponent, so a large part of her power depends on the player's ability to actually land these setups rather than raw kit strength alone.

Ivern.name: Ivern
Ivern.title: the Green Father
Ivern.blurb: Ivern Bramblefoot, known to many as the Green Father, is a peculiar half man, half tree who roams Runeterra's forests, cultivating life everywhere he goes. He knows the secrets of the natural world, and holds deep friendships with all things that grow...
Ivern.Notes: Ivern's passive (Friend of the Forest) makes jungle camps friendly to him instead of hostile, letting him clear the jungle quickly without taking damage and freeing him up to gank and support lanes early, effectively playing more like a roaming enchanter than a traditional jungler; his Q (Rootcaller) roots an enemy and pulls Ivern to them if it lands on a champion, his W (Triggerseed) shields an ally on a delay, and his ultimate (Daisy!) summons a powerful sentient golem that tanks and fights alongside him or an ally, giving him surprisingly strong peel and teamfight presence for a champion with very low personal combat stats and no real waveclear or dueling power of his own.

Janna.name: Janna
Janna.title: the Storm's Fury
Janna.blurb: Armed with the power of Runeterra's gales, Janna is a mysterious, elemental wind spirit who protects the dispossessed of Zaun. Some believe she was brought into existence by the pleas of Runeterra's sailors who prayed for fair winds as they navigated...
Janna.Notes: Janna's Q (Howling Gale) is a charge-up tornado that knocks up and damages enemies in its path, but the charge time telegraphs it and lets aware enemies dodge; her E (Eye of the Storm) shields an ally and boosts their attack damage, making her one of the premier peel/protect supports for hyper-carry ADCs, and her ultimate (Monsoon) is a massive AoE knockback plus strong healing zone, giving her some of the best disengage and teamfight-saving power in the game, but she has no self-mobility, no waveclear, and no way to lock enemies down for her team to capitalize on picks, making her a purely defensive/enabling support rather than an aggressive engage one.

JarvanIV.name: Jarvan IV
JarvanIV.title: the Exemplar of Demacia
JarvanIV.blurb: Prince Jarvan, scion of the Lightshield dynasty, is heir apparent to the throne of Demacia. Raised to be a paragon of his nation's greatest virtues, he is forced to balance the heavy expectations placed upon him with his own desire to fight on the front...
JarvanIV.Notes: Jarvan IV's signature combo drops his ultimate (Cataclysm) — an arena wall that isolates a target from allies — and then follows up with his E (Dragon Strike) dashing to that same spot to knock the trapped enemy up, creating one of the most reliable single-target burst/CC combos in the game for isolating a priority target in a skirmish or teamfight; his Q (Golden Aegis) grants an armor/magic-resist shield and slow on landing, adding to his engage/duel toolkit, but both his ult wall and E dash require precise combo execution and can be dodged or countered by displacement-immunity/dashes that let the target escape before the wall closes.

Jax.name: Jax
Jax.title: Grandmaster at Arms
Jax.blurb: Unmatched in both his skill with unique armaments and his biting sarcasm, Jax is the last known weapons master of Icathia. After his homeland was laid low by its own hubris in unleashing the Void, Jax and his kind vowed to protect what little remained...
Jax.Notes: Jax's E (Counter Strike) lets him dodge all incoming basic attacks for a brief window before stunning nearby enemies, making him one of the best answers to auto-attack-reliant champions and giving him a strong all-in tool once timed correctly; his passive (Relentless Assault) stacks bonus attack speed on consecutive autos, and his ultimate (Grandmaster's Might) grants bonus armor/magic resist plus AoE damage on his next attacks, making him a devastating scaling duelist and split-pusher, but his stun requires good read on when to activate the dodge window, and burst mages or CC-heavy ranged champions who don't rely on autos can punish him before he gets his combo online.

Jayce.name: Jayce
Jayce.title: the Defender of Tomorrow
Jayce.blurb: Jayce Talis is a brilliant inventor who, along with his friend Viktor, made the first great discoveries in the field of hextech. Celebrated across Piltover, he tries to live up to his reputation as "the Man of Progress," but often struggles with the...
Jayce.Notes: Jayce has no traditional ultimate — instead he transforms between Mercury Hammer (melee, with a leap-slam gap-closer that slows, and a point-blank knockback-root) and Mercury Cannon (ranged, with a poke skillshot that gains range/damage when fired through his speed-boosting Acceleration Gate), letting him flexibly poke from range then switch to melee to burst and finish a target up close. This dual-kit gives him some of the best all-in-or-disengage flexibility of any laner, but he has no sustain and a fairly demanding combo (E-Q gate-shot in ranged form, or leap-into-knockback in melee), so misplaying the stance swap or getting caught mid-transition leaves him vulnerable.

Jhin.name: Jhin
Jhin.title: the Virtuoso
Jhin.blurb: Jhin is a meticulous criminal psychopath who believes murder is art. Once an Ionian prisoner, but freed by shadowy elements within Ionia's ruling council, the serial killer now works as their cabal's assassin. Using his gun as his paintbrush, Jhin...
Jhin.Notes: Jhin's passive locks him to only 4 shots per clip, with the 4th always critically striking and dealing bonus damage — turning every fight into a rhythm of careful shot management rather than standard auto-attacking; his E (Captive Audience) plants invisible traps that root and reveal enemies who trigger them, giving him a way to set up his W (Deadly Flourish) root/execute from a distance, and his ultimate (Curtain Call) is a long-range, map-wide channeled cannon that can snipe low-health targets from an enormous distance, making him one of the best global-execute threats in the game; he has zero mobility and no escape, so if caught in melee range without his traps or team's peel, he's extremely vulnerable.

Jinx.name: Jinx
Jinx.title: the Loose Cannon
Jinx.blurb: An unhinged and impulsive criminal from the undercity, Jinx is haunted by the consequences of her past—but that doesn't stop her from bringing her own chaotic brand of pandemonium to Piltover and Zaun. She uses her arsenal of DIY weapons to devastating...
Jinx.Notes: Jinx's passive (Get Excited!) grants huge bonus attack speed and movement speed after a takedown or destroying a structure, letting her snowball hard and chain kills/objectives once she gets going; she swaps between her minigun (Pow-Pow, ramping attack speed for sustained DPS) and rocket launcher (Fishbones, AoE splash damage and bonus vs structures) via Q, giving her flexible waveclear and teamfight damage, and her E (Flame Chompers!) lays down traps that root anyone who triggers them, setting up her devastating long-range execute ultimate (Super Mega Death Rocket!) which deals more damage the farther it travels; she has no mobility or escape tools at all, however, making her fully reliant on peel and positioning to survive being caught out.

Kaisa.name: Kai'Sa
Kaisa.title: Daughter of the Void
Kaisa.blurb: Claimed by the Void when she was only a child, Kai'Sa managed to survive through sheer tenacity and strength of will. Her experiences have made her a deadly hunter and, to some, the harbinger of a future they would rather not live to see. Having entered...
Kaisa.Notes: Kai'Sa's Second Skin passive stacks bonus magic damage on abilities and evolves her Q/W/E individually based on which items she builds (crit, attack speed, or ability power), giving her a uniquely flexible build path that adapts to the game state; her ultimate (Killer Instinct) is a dash toward any marked ally or enemy champion (marks applied by her W or evolved passive), letting her engage onto a low-health target or reposition defensively toward a friendly, and if evolved it grants stealth during the dash, making her one of the safest and most explosive-scaling hyper-carries once she gets items online, though she has no traditional CC of her own and is fairly squishy/mana-light early before her evolves kick in.

Kalista.name: Kalista
Kalista.title: the Spear of Vengeance
Kalista.blurb: A specter of wrath and retribution, Kalista is the undying spirit of vengeance, an armored nightmare summoned from the Shadow Isles to hunt deceivers and traitors. The betrayed may cry out in blood to be avenged, but Kalista only answers those willing...
Kalista.Notes: Kalista's entire kit is built around her Oathsworn bond with an ally (usually her support) — her passive (Martial Poise) lets her mini-dash after every attack, making her exceptionally hard to hit with skillshots, while her E (Rend) stacks spears on-hit that she can detonate for a slowing burst, resetting on kills, which makes her devastating at contesting objectives like Dragon and Baron; her ultimate (Fate's Call) pulls her bound ally into a brief untargetable stasis and then launches them in a chosen direction, knocking up any enemies they collide with, turning any engage-oriented support into a surprise initiator or a clutch save tool — but this also means her ultimate is useless without her Oathsworn nearby, and losing that ally (or their input) removes a huge chunk of her kit's value.

Karma.name: Karma
Karma.title: the Enlightened One
Karma.blurb: No mortal exemplifies the spiritual traditions of Ionia more than Karma. She is the living embodiment of an ancient soul reincarnated countless times, carrying all her accumulated memories into each new life, and blessed with power that few can...
Karma.Notes: Karma's Mantra (R) is a resource-free empowerment mechanic rather than a traditional ultimate — it enhances her next basic ability, turning her Q into a bigger AoE slow-nuke, her W's root/tether into a wider bind that also shields allies caught in it, or her E's shield/speed into a stronger version that hits a bigger area — giving her constant access to a scaled-up spell rather than a single cooldown-gated ult; this makes her extremely flexible as either a poke-heavy solo laner or a shield/peel-focused support, but she has no mobility or escape of her own and no hard CC beyond her tether-root, so she's reliant on her range and cooldown management to stay safe.

Karthus.name: Karthus
Karthus.title: the Deathsinger
Karthus.blurb: The harbinger of oblivion, Karthus is an undying spirit whose haunting songs are a prelude to the horror of his nightmarish appearance. The living fear the eternity of undeath, but Karthus sees only beauty and purity in its embrace, a perfect union of...
Karthus.Notes: Karthus's ultimate (Requiem) is a global-range execute that damages every enemy champion on the map regardless of position, making him one of the best steal/finish tools for contested objectives, fights across the map, or securing kills on fleeing low-health targets anywhere; his passive (Death Defied) lets him continue casting spells for several seconds after dying, meaning he can still land a Requiem, Wall of Pain, or Defile tick even after being killed, and his E (Defile) toggles a mana-hungry AoE pulse around him that shreds waves and punishes enemies standing near him, giving him some of the best waveclear/zone pressure in the game; but he has zero mobility or escape, making him extremely vulnerable to being caught and killed quickly in lane or jungle before his ultimate/kit can scale.

Kassadin.name: Kassadin
Kassadin.title: the Void Walker
Kassadin.blurb: Cutting a burning swath through the darkest places of the world, Kassadin knows his days are numbered. A widely traveled Shuriman guide and adventurer, he had chosen to raise a family among the peaceful southern tribes—until the day his village was...
Kassadin.Notes: Kassadin's ultimate (Riftwalk) is a repeatable, low-cooldown blink that deals bonus damage on consecutive casts, making him one of the most mobile assassins/duelists once he's leveled 6 and stacked mana, and his Q (Null Sphere) both silences and blocks the first enemy projectile it collides with, giving him a strong answer to enemy poke/burst mages; he's infamous as one of the hardest-scaling champions in the game, historically weak and immobile before level 9 (when Riftwalk's cooldown drops enough to blink repeatedly) but capable of completely dominating a game if he gets there unpunished, so most of his identity revolves around surviving lane and then snowballing off his mobility advantage in the mid-late game.

Katarina.name: Katarina
Katarina.title: the Sinister Blade
Katarina.blurb: Decisive in judgment and lethal in combat, Katarina is a Noxian assassin of the highest caliber. Eldest daughter to the legendary General Du Couteau, she made her talents known with swift kills against unsuspecting enemies. Her fiery ambition has driven...
Katarina.Notes: Katarina's passive (Voracity) resets all of her ability cooldowns on a takedown, and her E (Shunpo) blinks her to an ally, enemy, or her own thrown dagger, letting her chain resets across multiple kills in a single fight; her ultimate (Death Lotus) channels rapid daggers at all nearby enemies simultaneously, dealing massive AoE damage if left uninterrupted, making her one of the best teamfight-swinging assassins when the enemy team is grouped, but she has zero CC of her own, and her ultimate channel can be interrupted by even a single stun/knockup/silence, so she relies entirely on her team creating an opening or a grouped, CC-free window for her to unleash it safely.

Kayle.name: Kayle
Kayle.title: the Righteous
Kayle.blurb: Born to a Targonian Aspect at the height of the Rune Wars, Kayle honored her mother's legacy by fighting for justice on wings of divine flame. She and her twin sister Morgana were the protectors of Demacia for many years—until Kayle became disillusioned...
Kayle.Notes: Kayle's passive/W (Divine Ascent) stacks up over the game and eventually transforms her from a melee-ish laner into a true ranged auto-attacker with bonus attack speed and range, meaning her early laning phase is a weak, awkward transition period she has to survive before she becomes a devastating scaling hyper-carry with strong waveclear and safety; her ultimate (Divine Judgment) can be cast on herself or any ally to grant temporary invulnerability (and later ranks add bonus damage/speed), making her one of the best anti-dive/anti-engage tools in the game for saving a teammate or herself from a burst combo or all-in, but she has no dash/blink of her own, so she's still reliant on positioning and her team's peel during her weaker early levels.

Kayn.name: Kayn
Kayn.title: the Shadow Reaper
Kayn.blurb: A peerless practitioner of lethal shadow magic, Shieda Kayn battles to achieve his true destiny—to one day lead the Order of Shadow into a new era of Ionian supremacy. He wields the sentient darkin weapon Rhaast, undeterred by its creeping corruption of...
Kayn.Notes: Kayn is unique in that his passive (The Darkin Scythe) lets him permanently choose one of two forms partway through the game based on whether he's damaged more melee or ranged champions — Shadow Assassin (extra mobility, bonus magic damage, resets on takedown) for cutting down squishies, or Rhaast (tankier, percent-max-health damage, heavy self-healing) for grinding down bruisers/tanks in extended fights — making his identity and matchups shift entirely partway through a game; his E (Shadow Step) lets him move through walls with bonus speed and healing, and his ultimate (Umbral Trespass) lets him infest a damaged enemy champion, becoming untargetable before bursting out with damage (and healing if Rhaast), giving him one of the best dive/all-in and tower-diving tools among junglers, though he has no hard CC of his own outside a W slow, so he leans on his team or his own burst/sustain rather than lockdown to win fights.

Kennen.name: Kennen
Kennen.title: the Heart of the Tempest
Kennen.blurb: More than just the lightning-quick enforcer of Ionian balance, Kennen is the only yordle member of the Kinkou. Despite his small, furry stature, he is eager to take on any threat with a whirling storm of shuriken and boundless enthusiasm. Alongside his...
Kennen.Notes: Kennen's passive (Mark of the Storm) stacks a debuff on enemies hit by his abilities or autos, and the third stack triggers a stun, which he can proc repeatedly on grouped enemies via his ultimate (Slicing Maelstrom), a channeled AoE pulse around him that can chain-stun an entire enemy team if they stay in range, making him one of the best teamfight-swinging AP-based bruisers/mages in the game once he gets into range of multiple targets; his E (Lightning Rush) turns him into an untargetable, unit-passing energy ball for a brief dash, letting him initiate or escape through the middle of a fight, but his stuns are entirely stack-dependent, so an aware enemy team can spread out or flee before hitting the third mark, and he has to actually get in range of his ultimate's pulses to make it count.

Khazix.name: Kha'Zix
Khazix.title: the Voidreaver
Khazix.blurb: The Void grows, and the Void adapts—in none of its myriad spawn are these truths more apparent than Kha'Zix. Evolution drives the core of this mutating horror, born to survive and to slay the strong. Where it struggles to do so, it grows new, more...
Khazix.Notes: Kha'Zix's entire kit revolves around his passive: any enemy without an allied champion or minion nearby counts as Isolated, and his Q (Taste Their Fear) deals dramatically increased damage against them, making him one of the best 1v1/split-lane duelists and backline-picking assassins when he can catch someone alone; at levels 6/11/16 he permanently evolves one of his four abilities (bonus range/cooldown refund on Q, a slowing 3-way cone on W, longer jumps with kill-resets on E, or extra stealth casts on his ultimate Void Assault), letting a player customize him toward dueling, poking, mobility, or repeated ambushes depending on the game state, but he has almost no real crowd control and very weak waveclear, so if he can't isolate a target or the fight happens near grouped allies, his damage output drops off substantially.

Kindred.name: Kindred
Kindred.title: The Eternal Hunters
Kindred.blurb: Separate, but never parted, Kindred represents the twin essences of death. Lamb's bow offers a swift release from the mortal realm for those who accept their fate. Wolf hunts down those who run from their end, delivering violent finality within his...
Kindred.Notes: Kindred's passive (Mark of the Kindred) lets Lamb hunt marked enemy champions and jungle camps, permanently gaining bonus attack range and empowered abilities for every completed hunt, giving her a distinct scaling/mini-game identity where finding and securing marks directly translates into power; her E (Mounting Dread) slows a target and, after landing 3 attacks on them, triggers a percent-missing-health execute via Wolf, and her signature ultimate (Lamb's Respite) creates a zone in which no unit — ally or enemy — can be reduced below 10% health or die, giving her one of the most unique clutch-save/anti-burst tools in the game to win extended trades, protect a dying ally, or safely secure a contested objective; but she has low sustain and no hard CC, so she has to actually out-position and out-kite opponents rather than lock them down.

Kled.name: Kled
Kled.title: the Cantankerous Cavalier
Kled.blurb: A warrior as fearless as he is ornery, the yordle Kled embodies the furious bravado of Noxus. He is an icon beloved by the empire's soldiers, distrusted by its officers, and loathed by the nobility. Many claim Kled has fought in every campaign the...
Kled.Notes: Kled effectively fights with two separate health bars — while Mounted on Skaarl, all damage is absorbed by his steed until it depletes, at which point he's forcibly Dismounted (losing his Q's pull, becoming weaker and slower, but gaining bonus movement speed toward visible enemies and resistances); he can fight his way back to full power by dealing damage to regain Courage and remount with a health refill, making him deceptively dangerous even when he appears to be losing a fight. His Q (Bear Trap on a Rope) pulls a hooked enemy toward him while mounted (replaced by a knockback pistol shot when dismounted), and his ultimate (Chaaaaaaaarge!!!) is a long-range charge that grants him and following allies a shield and speed boost, making it one of the best coordinated dive/engage tools in the game, though the charge-up telegraphs his approach and skilled teams can set up to counter it before he arrives.

KogMaw.name: Kog'Maw
KogMaw.title: the Mouth of the Abyss
KogMaw.blurb: Belched forth from a rotting Void incursion deep in the wastelands of Icathia, Kog'Maw is an inquisitive yet putrid creature with a caustic, gaping mouth. This particular Void-spawn needs to gnaw and drool on anything within reach to truly understand it...
KogMaw.Notes: Kog'Maw's W (Bio-Arcane Barrage) turns his basic attacks into true-damage missiles that shred through armor and tank builds, making him one of the best raw DPS hyper-carries once he's itemized, and his ultimate (Living Artillery) is a long-range bombardment that deals bonus damage based on the target's missing health, giving him strong poke/execute potential from well outside normal engage range; his passive (Icathian Surprise) causes him to explode for bonus damage after death, punishing enemies who don't finish him off from a safe distance, but he has zero mobility of any kind and is one of the most immobile ADCs in the game, making him entirely dependent on his team's peel and positioning to survive.

KSante.name: K'Sante
KSante.title: the Pride of Nazumah
KSante.blurb: Defiant and courageous, K'Sante battles colossal beasts and ruthless Ascended to protect his home of Nazumah, a coveted oasis amid the sands of Shurima. But after a falling-out with his former partner, K'Sante realizes that in order to become a warrior...
KSante.Notes: K'Sante's Q (Ntofo Strikes) scales its damage off bonus armor and magic resist rather than pure AD, meaning building tank items directly increases his damage output; landing two Q stacks unleashes a shockwave that pulls enemies in, and his W (Path Maker) is a charge-up dash that grants damage reduction and displacement immunity before ramming forward to knock back and stun everyone in its path — a strong anti-engage tool that can absorb burst combos entirely; his ultimate (All Out) transforms him into a more aggressive, mobile bruiser form where Path Maker instead deals bonus true damage and no longer stuns/knocks back, and his E (Footwork) becomes able to dash through walls, letting him isolate and displace a single enemy champion (potentially straight into his own team) for a devastating pick, though this transformation trades away some of his defensive identity for a burst all-in window.

Leblanc.name: LeBlanc
Leblanc.title: the Deceiver
Leblanc.blurb: Mysterious even to other members of the Black Rose cabal, LeBlanc is but one of many names for a pale woman who has manipulated people and events since the earliest days of Noxus. Using her magic to mirror herself, the sorceress can appear to anyone...
Leblanc.Notes: LeBlanc's Q (Sigil of Malice) marks a target, and any of her subsequent damaging abilities against that mark detonates it for bonus damage, forming the core of her burst combo; her E (Ethereal Chains) tethers a target and, if not broken, roots and re-damages them (also re-triggering the mark), and her W (Distortion) is a dash that leaves a return pad she can blink back to within a few seconds, giving her a genuine two-way escape/engage tool; her ultimate (Mimic) lets her recast any one of her three basic abilities a second time at reduced cost, meaning she can double up on whichever piece of her combo — extra burst, an extra root, or a second dash — making her deceptively flexible depending on the situation, though she's extremely squishy with no sustain, and hard CC or suppression that lands before she can use Distortion's return can leave her with no way out.

LeeSin.name: Lee Sin
LeeSin.title: the Blind Monk
LeeSin.blurb: A master of Ionia's ancient martial arts, Lee Sin is a principled fighter who channels the essence of the dragon spirit to face any challenge. Though he lost his sight many years ago, the warrior-monk has devoted his life to protecting his homeland...
LeeSin.Notes: Lee Sin's Q (Sonic Wave/Resonating Strike) is a skillshot dash-to-target combo that gives him excellent gap-closing and scouting, and he can dash to any ward he's placed, letting him make unpredictable engages or escapes from unusual angles; his W (Safeguard/Iron Will) is a dash to an ally that shields them both, doubling as an engage tool, a save for a teammate, or a repositioning move; and his ultimate (Dragon's Rage) is a kick that knocks the target back, knocking up and damaging anyone they collide with along the way, making it one of the most iconic playmaking tools in the game for peeling a diver off a carry or kicking an isolated enemy into his own team; but his damage and impact drop off significantly in the late game compared to scaling junglers, so he's most dangerous when snowballing an early lead.

Leona.name: Leona
Leona.title: the Radiant Dawn
Leona.blurb: Imbued with the fire of the sun, Leona is a holy warrior of the Solari who defends Mount Targon with her Zenith Blade and the Shield of Daybreak. Her skin shimmers with starfire while her eyes burn with the power of the celestial Aspect within her...
Leona.Notes: Leona's E (Zenith Blade) is a dash to an enemy that roots them if she was already close, and her Q (Shield of Daybreak) applies a guaranteed stun on her next auto-attack after casting, letting her chain a highly reliable engage combo; her ultimate (Solar Flare) is a delayed AoE stun that punishes grouped enemies, and her passive (Sunlight) marks enemies hit by her abilities so nearby allies deal bonus damage, making her one of the best all-in engage supports for setting up kills; but she has almost no personal damage or self-peel outside her CC chain, and her ultimate's stun requires enemies to still be in the zone when it detonates, so a coordinated enemy team can often walk out before it lands.

Lillia.name: Lillia
Lillia.title: the Bashful Bloom
Lillia.blurb: Intensely shy, the fae fawn Lillia skittishly wanders Ionia's forests. Hiding just out of sight of mortals—whose mysterious natures have long captivated, but intimidated, her—Lillia hopes to discover why their dreams no longer reach the ancient Dreaming...
Lillia.Notes: Lillia's passive (Dream-Laden Bough) applies Dream Dust to anything she hits, dealing percent-max-health magic damage over time and granting stacking movement speed on every landed ability, letting her weave in and out of fights with a hit-and-run playstyle; her Q (Blooming Blows) deals bonus true damage to enemies caught on the outer edge of its radius, making her an effective tank-shredder despite armor stacking, and her ultimate (Lilting Lullaby) can be cast from anywhere on the map to put every Dream-Dust-marked enemy champion to sleep simultaneously, setting up a devastating team-wide follow-up combo; but she has no mobility ability of her own (her speed comes from landing spells, not dashes), and her sleep requires enemies to already be tagged by Q or E beforehand, so she's weak before landing initial hits and can be caught out if she whiffs her setup.

Lissandra.name: Lissandra
Lissandra.title: the Ice Witch
Lissandra.blurb: Lissandra's magic twists the pure power of ice into something dark and terrible. With the force of her black ice, she does more than freeze—she impales and crushes those who oppose her. To the terrified denizens of the north, she is known only as ''The...
Lissandra.Notes: Lissandra's kit is built entirely around a short-range lockdown chain rather than poke: her E (Glacial Path) fires an ice claw she can teleport to, closing the distance despite otherwise having no mobility, her W (Ring of Frost) roots everyone in a small area around her, and her ultimate (Frozen Tomb) either stuns an enemy champion in place (dealing damage and slowing everyone nearby as the ice spreads) or, cast on herself, grants a self-stasis that heals her and makes her briefly untargetable — a strong defensive panic button on top of an all-in tool; her passive (Iceborn Subjugation) spawns a slowing, damage-dealing zombie clone whenever an enemy champion dies near her, giving her strong teamfight snowball potential off a single kill; but nearly her entire kit operates at close range, so she has to commit to melee-adjacent distance to do anything, and mobile burst mages who can punish that commitment are her toughest matchups.

Locke.name: Locke
Locke.title: the Ashen Exorcist
Locke.blurb: A nail-slinging exorcist versed in forbidden rites, Corvin Locke is the progeny of Demacian occultists. Born into lies and hypocrisy, he learned young that demons aren't the cause of humanity's darkness, but the consequence. Now, Locke tears through...
Locke.Notes: Locke uses his Q to throw nails to slow his targets. Stacks nails does extra damage when attack is proc-ed. His ultimate is easy to dodge or flash. Dying after being tagged by the ult leave behind a relic that Locke can pick up and gains additional permanent power.

Lucian.name: Lucian
Lucian.title: the Purifier
Lucian.blurb: Lucian, a Sentinel of Light, is a grim hunter of wraiths and specters, pursuing them relentlessly and annihilating them with his twin relic pistols. After the specter Thresh slew his wife, Lucian embarked on the path of vengeance—but even with her...
Lucian.Notes: Lucian's passive (Lightslinger) causes his next basic attack after casting an ability to fire twice, and every Lightslinger hit reduces the cooldown of his E (Relentless Pursuit), letting him weave abilities and dashes together for extremely high burst in short trading windows and for repeated repositioning in a single fight; his ultimate (The Culling) is a channeled rapid-fire barrage that he can move and reposition during (including dashing with E mid-channel), making it useful both as an execute/finisher and as sustained ranged pressure when it's unsafe to auto-attack; but he has no crowd control of his own and a notably short attack range for an ADC, so he relies heavily on his own combo timing and his team's peel/CC to convert his burst into kills and to survive being caught by ranged poke or all-ins.

Lulu.name: Lulu
Lulu.title: the Fae Sorceress
Lulu.blurb: The yordle mage Lulu is known for conjuring dreamlike illusions and fanciful creatures as she roams Runeterra with her fairy companion Pix. Lulu shapes reality on a whim, warping the fabric of the world, and what she views as the constraints of this...
Lulu.Notes: Lulu's W (Whimsy) can either polymorph an enemy — disabling their basic attacks and abilities entirely for a couple of seconds, a uniquely hard disable rather than a standard stun — or shrink/speed-boost an ally, and her E (Help, Pix!) shields and adds bonus damage to whichever ally she targets; her ultimate (Wild Growth) knocks up nearby enemies on cast and then grants the targeted ally significant bonus health and size for several seconds, making her one of the best protect-and-empower supports for turning her ADC into a nearly unkillable teamfight threat, but she has no self-mobility or personal combat strength, and enemies who can burst or lock her down before she can react tend to shut down her entire kit's value.

Lux.name: Lux
Lux.title: the Lady of Luminosity
Lux.blurb: Luxanna Crownguard hails from Demacia, an insular realm where magical abilities are viewed with fear and suspicion. Able to bend light to her will, she grew up dreading discovery and exile, and was forced to keep her power secret, in order to preserve...
Lux.Notes: Lux's passive (Illumination) marks enemies hit by her abilities, and her next damaging spell or auto against a marked target consumes it for bonus damage, rewarding chaining her kit together; her Q (Light Binding) is a root that can pierce through to hit two targets in a line, and her E (Lucent Singularity) creates a zone that slows enemies inside and can be detonated for extra damage, while her ultimate (Final Spark) fires an extremely long-range beam capable of hitting enemies from nearly across the map, making her one of the best long-range poke/execute mages in the game; but she has no mobility or escape tools whatsoever, and virtually her entire kit is skillshot-based, so a mobile diver who closes the distance and dodges her line abilities can shut her down quickly.

Malphite.name: Malphite
Malphite.title: Shard of the Monolith
Malphite.blurb: A massive creature of living stone, Malphite struggles to impose blessed order on a chaotic world. Birthed as a servitor-shard to an otherworldly obelisk known as the Monolith, he used his tremendous elemental strength to maintain and protect his...
Malphite.Notes: Malphet's ultimate ability can make or break team fights. Use it wisely and target carries.

Malzahar.name: Malzahar
Malzahar.title: the Prophet of the Void
Malzahar.blurb: A zealous seer dedicated to the unification of all life, Malzahar truly believes the newly emergent Void to be the path to Runeterra's salvation. In the desert wastes of Shurima, he followed the voices that whispered in his mind, all the way to ancient...
Malzahar.Notes: Malzahar's passive (Void Shift) grants immunity to crowd control and 90% damage reduction on the next hit if he hasn't taken damage recently, making him surprisingly hard to gank or burst down despite his complete lack of mobility; his E (Malefic Visions) is a strong damage-over-time nuke that spreads to a new target on a kill and refunds mana, and his ultimate (Nether Grasp) is a point-and-click suppression that fully locks down a champion for its duration — one of the few true suppresses in the game, un-dodgeable unlike a skillshot stun — making him one of the best answers to a fed or slippery enemy carry; but he is completely immobile with no dashes, blinks, or escapes of any kind, and his ultimate roots him in place while channeling, so a well-timed interrupt or hard engage before Void Shift is up can shut down his entire kit.

Maokai.name: Maokai
Maokai.title: the Twisted Treant
Maokai.blurb: Maokai is a rageful, towering treant who fights the unnatural horrors of the Shadow Isles. He was twisted into a force of vengeance after a magical cataclysm destroyed his home, surviving undeath only through the Waters of Life infused within his...
Maokai.Notes: Maokai's W (Twisted Advance) is an untargetable dash to an enemy that roots them on arrival, giving him a reliable single-target engage/peel tool, while his Q (Bramble Smash) sends a wall of brambles forward that roots whoever it collides with, useful for zoning or catching multiple enemies in a line; his E (Sapling Toss) provides vision and a delayed slow/damage detonation, and his ultimate (Vengeful Maelstrom) creates a shield around himself that absorbs and stores incoming damage before releasing it as an AoE nuke on expiration or recast, making him tanky and disruptive in extended teamfights; his passive (Sap Magic) also periodically empowers an auto-attack to heal him, giving him solid sustain in skirmishes, though his overall damage remains fairly modest without heavy investment, so he's primarily valued for his engage/peel and durability rather than as a damage carry.

MasterYi.name: Master Yi
MasterYi.title: the Wuju Bladesman
MasterYi.blurb: Master Yi has tempered his body and sharpened his mind, so that thought and action have become almost as one. Though he chooses to enter into violence only as a last resort, the grace and speed of his blade ensures resolution is always swift. As one of...
MasterYi.Notes: Master Yi's Q (Alpha Strike) blinks him through several enemies while making him briefly untargetable, letting him dodge skillshots, tower aggro, and even some ultimates entirely if timed well, and it resets Highlander's/Wuju Style's duration and refunds cooldown whenever it lands; his E (Wuju Style) adds bonus true damage on-hit, and his ultimate (Highlander) grants bonus attack/movement speed plus full immunity to slows, extending its duration on every takedown, making him one of the best snowballing clean-up carries in the game once teamfights are already messy — but he has zero crowd control of his own, is heavily reliant on his team creating chaos or landing CC for him to capitalize on, and hard CC that isn't a slow (stuns, roots, suppression) still stops him cold since Highlander only grants slow immunity, not general CC immunity.

Mel.name: Mel
Mel.title: the Soul's Reflection
Mel.blurb: Mel Medarda is the presumed heir of the Medarda family, once one of the most powerful in Noxus. In appearance she is a graceful aristocrat, but beneath the surface lies a skilled politician who makes it her business to know everything about everyone she...
Mel.Notes: Mel's passive (Searing Brilliance) grants bonus attack projectiles after casting a spell and applies a stacking, infinitely-scaling mark (Overwhelm/Death's Afterimage) on anything she damages, executing enemies outright once enough stacks accumulate; her W (Rebuttal) is a genuinely unique ability in League — a brief barrier that grants damage immunity and reflects incoming enemy projectiles (including some ultimates) back at their caster, and her E (Solar Snare) roots enemies caught in the center of its blast while slowing those on the edges, setting up her combo; her ultimate (Golden Eclipse) detonates every stack of Overwhelm on all marked enemies anywhere on the map without consuming them, making her a strong teamfight-closer and execute threat once she's tagged multiple targets, but she has no mobility or defensive tools for her team, and she's an artillery-style mage who has to actually land her setup and stack marks over an extended fight rather than winning through single burst combos.

Milio.name: Milio
Milio.title: The Gentle Flame
Milio.blurb: Milio is a warmhearted boy from Ixtal who has, despite his young age, mastered the fire axiom and discovered something new: soothing fire. With this newfound power, Milio plans to help his family escape their exile by joining the Yun Tal—just like his...
Milio.Notes: Milio's passive (Fired Up!) enchants allies touched by any of his abilities so their next attack deals bonus damage and burns the target, rewarding him for simply casting spells normally; his W (Cozy Campfire) drops a following zone that heals and grants bonus attack range to allies inside — a powerful siege/poke-enabling tool — his E (Warm Hugs) is a double-charge shield-plus-speed boost he can use on himself or an ally, and his ultimate (Breath of Life) heals and cleanses non-airborne crowd control from himself and nearby allies while granting tenacity, making him one of the best anti-CC-chain supports for freeing up a locked-down carry; but his only real offensive tool is Q (Ultra Mega Fire Kick), a single-target knockback-slow that's easy to dodge, so he contributes almost no personal kill pressure and is entirely dependent on his team's damage to close out fights.

MissFortune.name: Miss Fortune
MissFortune.title: the Bounty Hunter
MissFortune.blurb: A Bilgewater captain famed for her looks but feared for her ruthlessness, Sarah Fortune paints a stark figure among the hardened criminals of the port city. As a child, she witnessed the reaver king Gangplank murder her family—an act she brutally...
