MissFortune.Notes: Miss Fortune's passive (Love Tap) rewards switching targets by dealing bonus damage the first time she hits a new enemy, and her Q (Double Up) can be bounced off a minion to land guaranteed bonus damage on a champion standing behind it, making her one of the strongest early-lane bullies among ADCs; her E (Make It Rain) drops an uncleansable slow zone that grants vision, setting up her ultimate (Bullet Time), a channeled cone barrage that fires many waves of bullets and can single-handedly delete a grouped, slowed enemy team — but the channel roots her in place and can be fully interrupted by a single CC, and she has no mobility of her own, so hard engage or dive comps that can lock her down before or during Bullet Time shut down her entire kit.

MonkeyKing.name: Wukong
MonkeyKing.title: the Monkey King
MonkeyKing.blurb: Wukong is a vastayan trickster who uses his strength, agility, and intelligence to confuse his opponents and gain the upper hand. After finding a lifelong friend in the warrior known as Master Yi, Wukong became the last student of the ancient martial...
MonkeyKing.Notes: Wukong's W (Decoy) turns him invisible for a moment while leaving behind a clone that can also be re-triggered via his E (Nimbus Strike), letting him juke skillshots, escape ganks, or bait an enemy into wasting cooldowns on a fake target; his E is a short dash to an enemy that also hits others nearby, giving him a reliable gap-closer/reset tool for chasing or engaging, and his ultimate (Cyclone) grows in size as he spins, dealing damage and knocking up all nearby enemies before granting him bonus attack damage, making him one of the best AoE engage tools for diving onto a grouped enemy team; but his kit is fairly all-in and telegraphed once he commits to Cyclone, and he has no ranged tools or hard CC outside his ultimate, so kiting champions or those who can interrupt his spin can neutralize his combo before it lands.

Mordekaiser.name: Mordekaiser
Mordekaiser.title: the Iron Revenant
Mordekaiser.blurb: Twice slain and thrice born, Mordekaiser is a brutal warlord from a foregone epoch who uses his necromantic sorcery to bind souls into an eternity of servitude. Few now remain who remember his earlier conquests, or know the true extent of his powers—but...
Mordekaiser.Notes: Mordekaiser's ultimate (Realm of Death) banishes a single enemy champion into an isolated dimension for a forced 7-second 1v1, stealing a portion of their stats and letting no one else interfere — making him one of the best duelist/pick tools in the game for removing a key threat from a teamfight entirely; his passive (Indestructible) stores a percentage of damage dealt and taken as a growing shield he can pop and later convert into healing, giving him excellent sustain in extended fights, and his E (Death's Grasp) pulls enemies toward him to close gaps against ranged targets, but he was famously the only champion with zero mobility and crowd control for years, and even now his kit remains almost entirely about storing damage, pulling, and isolating rather than traditional CC, so mobile or true-damage-heavy duelists who can kite him or ignore his shield stacking tend to give him the most trouble.

Morgana.name: Morgana
Morgana.title: the Fallen
Morgana.blurb: Conflicted between her celestial and mortal natures, Morgana bound her wings to embrace humanity, and inflicts her pain and bitterness upon the dishonest and the corrupt. She rejects laws and traditions she believes are unjust, and fights for truth from...
Morgana.Notes: Morgana's E (Black Shield) is one of the most impactful defensive tools in the game — it blocks all incoming crowd control and a large amount of damage from the next enemy spell, making her a premier answer to hard-CC engage compositions and a key protector for her carries; her Q (Dark Binding) is a precise root skillshot that's difficult to land but sets up a strong follow-up, and her ultimate (Soul Shackles) tethers to nearby enemies and stuns them if they fail to break free before it expires, giving her strong teamfight lockdown once she's in range; but she has no mobility and relatively low sustain outside her passive's spell-vamp, so she has to play safely at range and rely on Black Shield to survive dives rather than escaping them.

Naafiri.name: Naafiri
Naafiri.title: the Hound of a Hundred Bites
Naafiri.blurb: Across the sands of Shurima, a chorus of howls rings out. It is the call of the dune hounds, voracious predators who form packs and compete for the right to hunt in these barren lands. Among them, one pack stands above all, for they are driven not only...
Naafiri.Notes: Naafiri's passive summons Packmates — spectral dogs that mirror her attacks and abilities for bonus damage — and her kit is unusually mobility-dense: her E (Eviscerate) is a dash that recalls and fully heals her Packmates, her W (The Call of the Pack) is a burst-empower that spawns extra Packmates and grants speed/vision, and her ultimate (Hounds' Pursuit) is a channeled dash-execute where she and her whole pack single out and lunge at one target simultaneously, refunding itself for a follow-up recast if she scores a takedown, letting her chain kills across a fight; she has almost no traditional CC beyond a brief, near-total slow on her ultimate's impact, so she wins fights through raw burst damage, mobility, and snowballing off picks rather than lockdown.

Nami.name: Nami
Nami.title: the Tidecaller
Nami.blurb: A headstrong young vastaya of the seas, Nami was the first of the Marai tribe to leave the waves and venture onto dry land, when their ancient accord with the Targonians was broken. With no other option, she took it upon herself to complete the sacred...
Nami.Notes: Nami's Q (Aqua Prison) is a hard-hitting root/stun skillshot bubble that's difficult to land at range but devastating when it does, and her W (Ebb and Flow) bounces between an ally and enemy, healing her team while damaging the enemy on each bounce, letting her poke and sustain simultaneously; her ultimate (Tidal Wave) is an AoE line knockup-and-slow useful both for engage and peel, and her E (Tidecaller's Blessing) empowers an ally's next several auto-attacks to deal bonus damage on enemies on hit, — making her one of the best engage-enabling supports when paired with a follow-up carry, though she has no self-mobility or escape, so she's vulnerable if her own positioning goes wrong.

Nasus.name: Nasus
Nasus.title: the Curator of the Sands
Nasus.blurb: Nasus is an imposing, jackal-headed Ascended being from ancient Shurima, a heroic figure regarded as a demigod by the people of the desert. Fiercely intelligent, he was a guardian of knowledge and peerless strategist whose wisdom guided the ancient...
Nasus.Notes: Nasus's Q (Siphoning Strike) permanently gains bonus damage every time it lands a killing blow, so his damage output scales infinitely with how much he stacks it over the course of a game, letting a well-farmed Nasus one-shot squishies and shred towers late; his W (Wither) is a devastating single-target slow that also cripples attack speed and ramps up in severity over its duration, making him one of the best anti-kiting tools for locking down a fleeing or kiting enemy carry, and his ultimate (Fury of the Sands) grants him bonus health, resistances, size, and range while dealing AoE damage around him and halving Siphoning Strike's cooldown, turning him into a genuine teamfight/split-push threat once stacked; but he lacks mobility and hard CC beyond Wither, making him relatively easy to kite, and he isn't particularly strong in messy teamfights since Fury of the Sands requires him to be in melee range to matter,  so his real strength is split-pushing and 1v1 dueling rather than group fighting.

Nautilus.name: Nautilus
Nautilus.title: the Titan of the Depths
Nautilus.blurb: A lonely legend as old as the first piers sunk in Bilgewater, the armored goliath known as Nautilus roams the dark waters off the coast of the Blue Flame Isles. Driven by a forgotten betrayal, he strikes without warning, swinging his enormous anchor to...
Nautilus.Notes: Nautilus's Q (Dredge Line) pulls himself toward a hit champion (or to terrain, letting him reposition or escape), and his passive (Staggering Blow) roots the first target he auto-attacks after a cooldown, forming one of the most reliable engage combos in the game — hook in, auto-stun, then slow with E (Riptide) while W (Titan's Wrath) shields him and adds bonus on-hit damage; his ultimate (Depth Charge) fires a chasing shockwave that knocks up and stuns everyone near its target when it erupts, making him excellent both for diving a backline target and for punishing a grouped enemy team. He has four separate forms of CC across his kit, giving him some of the best all-in and pick potential of any engage support/tank, but his Q can be blocked by minions and his lack of any other mobility outside the hook means positioning matters heavily.

Neeko.name: Neeko
Neeko.title: the Curious Chameleon
Neeko.blurb: Hailing from a long lost tribe of vastaya, Neeko can blend into any crowd by borrowing the appearances of others, even absorbing something of their emotional state to tell friend from foe in an instant. No one is ever sure where—or who—Neeko might be...
Neeko.Notes: Neeko's passive (Inherent Glamour) lets her disguise herself as an allied champion, deceiving the enemy team about her real position or identity — a genuinely unique mechanic she can use to bait dives, fake being an ally, or hide her ultimate's windup entirely; her E (Tangle-Barbs) is a piercing skillshot that roots everyone it passes through, with the root growing longer the more targets it hits, and her ultimate (Pop Blossom) has a telegraphed wind-up before she leaps and slams down, stunning and damaging everyone caught in the blast — a devastating teamfight-ending combo when set up properly with her E or while disguised to catch the enemy off guard; but she has no personal mobility or escape outside her W's brief stealth-and-clone trick, so if her disguise is seen through or her combo whiffs, she's very exposed.

Nidalee.name: Nidalee
Nidalee.title: the Bestial Huntress
Nidalee.blurb: Raised in the deepest jungle, Nidalee is a master tracker who can shapeshift into a ferocious cougar at will. Neither wholly woman nor beast, she viciously defends her territory from any and all trespassers, with carefully placed traps and deft spear...
Nidalee.Notes: Nidalee's kit swaps between Human form (Javelin Toss, a long-range spear that deals more damage the farther it travels, plus Bushwhack traps that reveal and damage) and Cougar form (Takedown, an execute that deals more damage the lower the target's health, plus Pounce, a mobility leap), letting her poke from range then transform to finish a target in melee; her passive (Prowl/Hunt) grants bonus movement speed in brush and toward marked enemies, giving her exceptional catch potential, and her ultimate (Aspect of the Cougar) is simply the form-swap itself, usable from level 1 — but she has no crowd control of any kind in her entire kit,  making her purely a damage/mobility/vision threat who relies on execute damage and picks rather than lockdown, and she falls off significantly in the late game compared to scaling junglers.

Nilah.name: Nilah
Nilah.title: the Joy Unbound
Nilah.blurb: Nilah is an ascetic warrior from a distant land, seeking the world's deadliest, most titanic opponents so that she might challenge and destroy them. Having won her power through an encounter with the long-imprisoned demon of joy, she has no emotions...
Nilah.Notes: Nilah's passive (Joy Unending) amplifies and shares healing/shielding with nearby allies, meaning any heal she or a teammate receives gets boosted for both, while her Q (Formless Blade) lifesteal and W (Jubilant Veil) — which grants ghosting and dodges all incoming basic attacks, extending the effect to any ally she touches — give her one of the strongest sustain/dodge kits among ADCs; her E (Slipstream) is a repeatable dash through a target with two charges, and her ultimate (Apotheosis) is a whirling AoE burst that pulls nearby enemies toward her at the final hit while healing her and nearby allies, making her a genuine teamfight-anchor melee ADC rather than a backline poke carry — but as a melee marksman she has to get in close to deal damage, and ranged ADCs who can kite and poke her down before she closes the gap remain her toughest matchups.

Nocturne.name: Nocturne
Nocturne.title: the Eternal Nightmare
Nocturne.blurb: A demonic amalgamation drawn from the nightmares that haunt every sentient mind, the thing known as Nocturne has become a primordial force of pure evil. It is liquidly chaotic in aspect, a faceless shadow with cold eyes and armed with wicked-looking...
Nocturne.Notes: Nocturne's ultimate (Paranoia) has two parts — it globally nearsights every enemy champion on the map, then lets him dash with displacement immunity to any visible enemy champion from an enormous distance, making him a devastating pick-and-delete threat once he can see an isolated target; his E (Unspeakable Horror) tethers a target and, if they fail to break it, fears and heavily slows them while granting him bonus movement speed toward feared enemies, forming a near-inescapable lock once it lands, and his W (Shroud of Darkness) is both a passive attack-speed steroid and an active spell shield that blocks the next enemy ability — successfully blocking a key spell doubles his attack speed for several seconds, making it a strong direct counter to peel/CC-reliant escape tools; but his kit is heavily reliant on isolating a single target, and champions whose kit doesn't hinge on a blockable spell, or who can simply out-brawl him in a straight fight, remain problematic.

Nunu.name: Nunu & Willump
Nunu.title: the Boy and His Yeti
Nunu.blurb: Once upon a time, there was a boy who wanted to prove he was a hero by slaying a fearsome monster—only to discover that the beast, a lonely and magical yeti, merely needed a friend. Bound together by ancient power and a shared love of snowballs, Nunu...
Nunu.Notes: Nunu & Willump's W (Biggest Snowball Ever!) is a growing, gap-closing snowball that knocks up anything it collides with, letting them gank or engage from unusual angles, and their E (Snowball Barrage) throws volleys that mark and slow targets before Willump roots any marked enemies nearby a few seconds later, forming a strong CC chain into their ultimate (Absolute Zero) — a channeled blizzard that shields them and progressively slows nearby enemies before exploding for massive damage based on channel time, making it one of the best zone-denial/teamfight ultimates in the game when landed on a grouped or CC-locked enemy team; their passive (Consume) also gives them the fastest jungle clear and objective-securing speed of any jungler via true damage to monsters — but their success depends heavily on team conversion: hitting the snowball or landing the ultimate does nothing if allies don't follow up, and a well-timed engage can become a wasted sacrifice if the team doesn't capitalize on the window created.

Olaf.name: Olaf
Olaf.title: the Berserker
Olaf.blurb: An unstoppable force of destruction, the axe-wielding Olaf wants nothing but to die in glorious combat. Hailing from the brutal Freljordian peninsula of Lokfar, he once received a prophecy foretelling his peaceful passing—a coward's fate, and a great...
Olaf.Notes: Olaf's passive (Berserker Rage) grants him massive attack speed the lower his health drops, and his W (Vicious Strikes) amplifies healing from all sources scaled by missing health, making him one of the tankiest-feeling duelists in the game when low — his E (Reckless Swing) deals true damage to both himself and the target (refunding the health cost if it kills), letting him shred through armor stacking, and his ultimate (Ragnarok) cleanses all current crowd control and grants full CC immunity for its duration, extended by every landed auto-attack or Reckless Swing — making him nearly impossible to peel off a target once he commits, and one of the best answers to CC-heavy team compositions in the game; but his only real crowd control is a slow-projectile axe (Undertow) that's easy to dodge and can be denied by preventing him from picking it back up, and he has no mobility outside of chasing on foot, so purely kiting, ranged champions who never let him close the gap remain his hardest matchups.

Orianna.name: Orianna
Orianna.title: the Lady of Clockwork
Orianna.blurb: Once a curious girl of flesh and blood, Orianna is now a technological marvel comprised entirely of clockwork. She became gravely ill after an accident in the lower districts of Zaun, and her failing body had to be replaced with exquisite artifice...
Orianna.Notes: Orianna's entire kit revolves around The Ball, a controllable pet she repositions with Q (Command: Attack), then triggers with W (Command: Dissonance, a damage/slow-vs-haste pulse) or E (Command: Protect, a shield that damages enemies in transit and grants bonus resistances to whoever it's attached to); her ultimate (Command: Shockwave) detonates The Ball after a brief delay, pulling and damaging every nearby enemy — one of the best teamfight-swinging AoE ultimates in the game if she catches a grouped enemy team, and often set up by attaching The Ball to an engaging frontline ally so the pull originates from deep in the enemy formation; but she has no personal mobility or escape, and virtually all of her impact depends on correctly positioning The Ball, making her vulnerable to anyone who can close the gap and burst her down before she can reposition it.

Ornn.name: Ornn
Ornn.title: The Fire below the Mountain
Ornn.blurb: Ornn is the Freljordian spirit of forging and craftsmanship. He works in the solitude of a massive smithy, hammered out from the lava caverns beneath the volcano Hearth-Home. There he stokes bubbling cauldrons of molten rock to purify ores and fashion...
Ornn.Notes: Ornn's passive (Living Forge) lets him build items from anywhere on the map without recalling and, from level 13, upgrade Legendary items into Masterwork versions for both himself and teammates, giving him unique lane-sustain and late-game itemization power; his Q (Volcanic Rupture) creates a magma pillar that his E (Searing Charge) can then ram into for a bonus knockup, and his W (Bellows Breath) applies Brittle, a debuff that empowers his and allies' next immobilizing effect or auto-attack against the target — his ultimate (Call of the Forge God) summons a stampeding lava elemental that he can redirect by dashing into it, knocking up anything in its new path, making him one of the most CC-dense tanks in the game once his combo pieces are chained together, though virtually everything requires either landing a skillshot or correctly timing his terrain interactions, and he lacks personal mobility outside his combat abilities, struggling badly in 1v1s against sustained, mobile duelists.

Pantheon.name: Pantheon
Pantheon.title: the Unbreakable Spear
Pantheon.blurb: Once an unwilling host to the Aspect of War, Atreus survived when the celestial power within him was slain, refusing to succumb to a blow that tore stars from the heavens. In time, he learned to embrace the power of his own mortality, and the stubborn...
Pantheon.Notes: Pantheon's W (Shield Vault) is a point-and-click dash-stun onto a target champion, forming the start of nearly every trade, and his passive (Mortal Will) empowers his next attack to strike three times or buffs his next spell every few casts, rewarding aggressive ability weaving; his E (Aegis Assault) makes him briefly invulnerable to damage from the front while dealing continuous damage in a cone — a strong trading and even tower-diving tool since he can block a turret shot or two — and his ultimate (Grand Starfall) is a long channel-then-leap that lets him land almost anywhere on the map, making him one of the best semi-global roaming/dive ultimates in the game for joining a fight from an unexpected angle; but he falls off significantly in the late game since his damage doesn't scale as well as other bruisers, so his identity is almost entirely about winning the early game hard and then using his global presence to keep impacting fights he can't win through raw stats alone.

Poppy.name: Poppy
Poppy.title: Keeper of the Hammer
Poppy.blurb: Runeterra has no shortage of valiant champions, but few are as tenacious as Poppy. Bearing the legendary hammer of Orlon, a weapon twice her size, this determined yordle has spent untold years searching in secret for the fabled “Hero of Demacia,” said...
Poppy.Notes: Poppy's W (Steadfast Presence) grounds nearby enemy dashes — stopping and slowing any enemy who tries to dash toward or away from her — making her one of the strongest counters in the game to mobility-reliant champions, and her E (Heroic Charge) carries a target forward, stunning them if they collide with terrain; her ultimate (Keeper's Verdict) can be charged for extra range and knocks enemies back an enormous distance toward their own fountain (or knocks up if no one is in front of her, firing a shockwave instead), making it both a devastating peel tool for saving an ally and a game-ending pick if it catches a priority target alone; but her identity is fundamentally reactive and anti-mobility rather than a pure engage tool, so she struggles most against champions whose escape isn't a simple dash — like blinks that bypass Steadfast Presence entirely, or ranged disengage that can interrupt her channeled ultimate before it goes off.

Pyke.name: Pyke
Pyke.title: the Bloodharbor Ripper
Pyke.blurb: A renowned harpooner from the slaughter docks of Bilgewater, Pyke should have met his death in the belly of a gigantic jaull-fish… and yet, he returned. Now, stalking the dank alleys and backways of his former hometown, he uses his new supernatural...
Pyke.Notes: Pyke's Q (Bone Skewer) can be tapped as a slow or charged into a harpoon that pulls the first enemy hit toward him, and his E (Phantom Undertow) is a dash that leaves a phantom which returns a second later, stunning everyone it passes through — chaining Q into E is his core kill combo, and E can also cross terrain, making it a strong escape/repositioning tool as well as an engage one; his passive (Gift of the Drowned Ones) heals him for stored damage whenever he's unseen by enemies (triggered by camouflage or brush) and converts any bonus health into attack damage, letting him play as a durable assassin rather than a traditional peel/enchanter support; his ultimate (Death from Below) executes low-health enemies in an X-shaped area and can be recast for free if it lands a kill, granting bonus gold to the last ally who assisted — making him a genuinely unique 'assassin support' whose entire identity revolves around picking off targets and sharing the resulting gold rather than protecting or enabling a carry directly.

Qiyana.name: Qiyana
Qiyana.title: Empress of the Elements
Qiyana.blurb: In the jungle city of Ixaocan, Qiyana plots her own ruthless path to the high seat of the Yun Tal. Last in line to succeed her parents, she faces those who stand in her way with brash confidence and unprecedented mastery over elemental magic. With the...
Qiyana.Notes: Qiyana's kit revolves around attuning to one of three terrain types via W (Terrashape, a short dash-to-terrain that also empowers her stats) — River grants her Q a root-then-slow, Brush grants stealth and speed, and Terrain grants bonus execute damage — letting her adapt her combo entirely to her surroundings, and her passive (Royal Privilege) resets every time she changes elements, allowing her to re-proc bonus damage on the same target multiple times per fight; her E (Audacity) is a short dash that can be cast mid-cast to auto-aim her Q at the dash target, guaranteeing the elemental effect connects, and her ultimate (Supreme Display of Talent) sends a windblast that knocks back enemies and, upon passing through river, brush, or terrain, erupts into a shockwave that stuns and heavily damages everyone caught in it — making river/jungle skirmishes near terrain especially deadly for her; but she has no true escape outside her Brush stealth, and champions who can suppress her, blink away from her E-Q combo, or simply out-scale her burst in the late game (since she falls off compared to hyper-carry ADCs) give her the most trouble.

Quinn.name: Quinn
Quinn.title: Demacia's Wings
Quinn.blurb: Quinn is an elite ranger-knight of Demacia, who undertakes dangerous missions deep in enemy territory. She and her legendary eagle, Valor, share an unbreakable bond, and their foes are often slain before they realize they are fighting not one, but two...
Quinn.Notes: Quinn's passive (Harrier) has Valor periodically mark a nearby enemy, and any of her damaging abilities (Q, E, or ultimate) also apply the mark, empowering her next auto-attack against that target for bonus damage; her Q (Blinding Assault) nearsights the primary target while damaging everyone nearby, and her E (Vault) dashes to a target, slows them, and then leaps back to max attack range — a hit-and-run combo that lets her poke safely; her ultimate (Behind Enemy Lines) transforms her into a flying, high-speed skirmisher for map-crossing mobility and can be ended early with Skystrike, an AoE nuke that marks everyone hit — making her one of the best roaming, split-pushing, and isolated-pick champions in the game, though she has no hard CC and very little sustain, so she has to rely on her nearsight/mark combo and repositioning to win fights rather than committing to prolonged skirmishes.

Rakan.name: Rakan
Rakan.title: The Charmer
Rakan.blurb: As mercurial as he is charming, Rakan is an infamous vastayan troublemaker and the greatest battle-dancer in Lhotlan tribal history. To the humans of the Ionian highlands, his name has long been synonymous with wild festivals, uncontrollable parties...
Rakan.Notes: Rakan's W (Grand Entrance) dashes him to a location and knocks up nearby enemies after a brief delay, and his ultimate (The Quickness) grants a burst of ghosted movement speed while charming and slowing every enemy champion he touches — combining the two lets him charm a target first (preventing dashes/flashes to dodge) and then guarantee the knockup, one of the most reliable engage combos among supports; his E (Battle Dance) is a repeatable dash-to-ally that shields them (with extended range and a stronger shield if the ally is Xayah, his canonical bot-lane partner), giving him excellent mobility to engage, peel, or escape almost instantly; but all of his abilities are dashes/skillshots that can be dodged or interrupted mid-cast, and outside of combos with allies he has very little raw damage or waveclear, making him almost entirely reliant on his mobility and CC-chain to create value.

Rammus.name: Rammus
Rammus.title: the Armordillo
Rammus.blurb: Idolized by many, dismissed by some, mystifying to all, the curious being Rammus is an enigma. Protected by a spiked shell, he inspires increasingly disparate theories on his origin wherever he goes—from demigod, to sacred oracle, to a mere beast...
Rammus.Notes: Rammus's E (Frenzying Taunt) is a point-and-click, un-dodgeable taunt that forces a target to attack him — one of the longest single-target hard-CC durations in the game at max rank — and pairs devastatingly with his W (Defensive Ball Curl), which massively boosts his armor/magic resist and reflects damage back at attackers, meaning a taunted AD carry effectively kills itself trying to fight him; his Q (Powerball) is a self-propelled rolling dash that gains speed and slows on impact, and his ultimate (Soaring Slam) is a leap with crowd-control immunity during the jump that slows on landing (and knocks up as well if cast while still rolling from Powerball), giving him strong burst engage range, especially since Powerball's speed extends Soaring Slam's cast range dramatically; his passive (Spiked Shell) also converts his stacked resistances into bonus attack damage, meaning the tankier he builds, the harder he hits — but he has almost no self-sustain and his damage remains entirely dependent on his defensive stats, so percent-health or true-damage-heavy champions who don't rely on basic attacks can bypass his taunt-punish gimmick entirely.

RekSai.name: Rek'Sai
RekSai.title: the Void Burrower
RekSai.blurb: An apex predator, Rek'Sai is a merciless Void-spawn that tunnels beneath the ground to ambush and devour unsuspecting prey. Her insatiable hunger has laid waste to entire regions of the once-great empire of Shurima—merchants, traders, even armed...
RekSai.Notes: Rek'Sai's passive lets her toggle between Unburrowed (auto-attack based, with Furious Bite dealing bonus true damage at max Fury) and Burrowed form (increased move speed, reduced vision, and a Tunnel that creates a reusable long-lasting tunnel entrance she can travel between); casting Unburrow while underground knocks up and damages nearby enemies, giving her a strong ambush-engage tool, and her ultimate (Void Rush) passively marks any enemy she's damaged, then lets her vanish underground briefly (displacement-immune and untargetable) before blinking to and pouncing on the marked target for bonus damage based on their max health — making her one of the best skirmish/duel/ambush junglers in the game; but her tunnels can be destroyed by enemies standing on the entrances, and she has notably low waveclear and falls off in the late game compared to scaling junglers, so her value is heavily front-loaded into early-game skirmishes, ganks, and objective control.

Rell.name: Rell
Rell.title: the Iron Maiden
Rell.blurb: The product of brutal experimentation at the hands of the Black Rose, Rell is a defiant, living weapon determined to topple Noxus. Her childhood was one of misery and horror, enduring unspeakable procedures to perfect and weaponize her magical control...
Rell.Notes: Rell toggles between a fast Mounted form and a tankier, slower Dismounted form via her W (Ferromancy) — Crash Down leaps off her mount to knock up and stun a wide area, while Mount Up (cast while dismounted) charges forward and flips the next enemy she attacks, remounting her; her E (Attract and Repel) binds her to an ally, letting her recast it to stun everyone caught between them, and her ultimate (Magnet Storm) yanks nearby enemies toward her instantly before continuously dragging them closer for a couple seconds, forming one of the biggest team-wide CC chains in the game when stacked with her W and E; her passive (Break the Mold) steals armor/MR from enemies she damages, and her Q (Shattering Strike) breaks enemy shields, giving her a strong anti-tank and anti-shield niche — but her CC-heavy, all-or-nothing kit leaves her extremely vulnerable if her engage whiffs, especially in her slow Dismounted state, and enemies with disengage or spell-shields can neutralize her combo before it lands.

Renata.name: Renata Glasc
Renata.title: the Chem-Baroness
Renata.blurb: Renata Glasc rose from the ashes of her childhood home with nothing but her name and her parents' alchemical research. In the decades since, she has become Zaun's wealthiest chem-baron, a business magnate who built her power by tying everyone's...
Renata.Notes: Renata's ultimate (Hostile Takeover) forces every enemy champion hit to go Berserk — attacking whatever is nearest, prioritizing their own allies first — making it one of the most disruptive AoE crowd control effects in the game if it catches a grouped enemy team; her Q (Handshake) roots the first enemy hit and can be recast to throw them in a direction, stunning them if they collide with something (or with an enemy champion) — useful both as an engage hook and as a way to reposition an ally out of danger; her W (Bailout) buffs an ally with ramping attack/move speed and, if they'd otherwise die while it's active, restores them to full health with a burning death timer that can only be canceled by getting a takedown — a unique 'second wind' mechanic that snowballs fed carries especially hard; her passive (Leverage) marks enemies on-hit so allies deal bonus damage to them, and her E (Loyalty Program) both shields allies and slows/damages enemies in its path — but she has zero personal mobility and very low overall tankiness, meaning she's an easy kill target if caught alone, and her engage tools rely on landing skillshots rather than guaranteed point-and-click CC.

Renekton.name: Renekton
Renekton.title: the Butcher of the Sands
Renekton.blurb: Renekton is a terrifying, rage-fueled Ascended being from the scorched deserts of Shurima. Once, he was his empire's most esteemed warrior, leading the nation's armies to countless victories. However, after the empire's fall, Renekton was entombed...
Renekton.Notes: Renekton's kit revolves around Fury, a resource generated by autos, abilities, and taking damage — at 50+ Fury his Q (Cull the Meek) heals for far more and his W (Ruthless Predator) strikes three times instead of two, stunning longer and shredding any shields on the target, making Fury management the core of his combo; his E (Slice and Dice) is a double-dash that shreds armor on the second hit and resets his auto-attack timer, giving him excellent gap-close and escape tools, and his ultimate (Dominus) instantly grants a large chunk of bonus health, increased size/range, and passive Fury generation for its duration, letting him turn losing fights into sudden comebacks; this combination of instant sustain, reliable stun, and burst damage makes him one of the strongest lane bullies and 1v1 duelists in the game early, though he has a naturally high health pool that makes him vulnerable to percent-health damage, and burst mages or ranged kiting champions who can punish him from range remain his toughest matchups.

Rengar.name: Rengar
Rengar.title: the Pridestalker
Rengar.blurb: Rengar is a ferocious vastayan trophy hunter who lives for the thrill of tracking down and killing dangerous creatures. He scours the world for the most fearsome beasts he can find, especially seeking any trace of Kha'Zix, the void creature who...
Rengar.Notes: Rengar's Ferocity resource builds with every ability cast (or first attack while leaping from brush via his passive, Unseen Predator), and at max stacks his next ability becomes empowered — Savagery hits harder with attack speed, Battle Roar heals him substantially and cleanses/blocks incoming CC, and Bola Strike roots instead of just slowing; his ultimate (Thrill of the Hunt) grants camouflage and reveals nearby enemy champions to him while letting him leap from anywhere (not just brush), making him one of the best pure-ambush assassins for isolating and one-shotting a squishy target; his Bonetooth Necklace also grants permanent bonus AD for unique champion takedowns, rewarding aggressive snowballing, but he trades poorly at low Ferocity, is highly vulnerable to blinds since his damage is heavily auto-attack-reliant, and struggles in large teamfights since his kit is entirely built around picking off isolated targets rather than group fighting.

Riven.name: Riven
Riven.title: the Exile
Riven.blurb: Once a swordmaster in the warhosts of Noxus, Riven is an expatriate in a land she previously tried to conquer. She rose through the ranks on the strength of her conviction and brutal efficiency, and was rewarded with a legendary runic blade and a...
Riven.Notes: Riven's Q (Broken Wings) can be cast up to three times in quick succession, each slash resetting her auto-attack timer, with the third cast crossing terrain and knocking up nearby enemies, and her W (Ki Burst) is a fast, small-radius AoE stun; her E (Valor) is a shielding dash that (unlike Q's third cast) cannot cross terrain, giving her constant mobility to chain abilities, dodge skillshots, or reposition; her passive (Runic Blade) charges from ability casts and empowers her next basic attacks with bonus damage, rewarding tight animation-canceling and ability weaving; her ultimate (Blade of the Exile) grants bonus AD, range, and a single cast of Wind Slash — a cone execute that deals dramatically more damage the lower the target's health, perfect for finishing a fleeing or low-health enemy — making her one of the highest-skill-ceiling, highest-mobility duelists in the game, but she has zero self-sustain outside her shield, so sustain-heavy or true-damage duelists who can outlast her burst window are her toughest matchups.

Rumble.name: Rumble
Rumble.title: the Mechanized Menace
Rumble.blurb: Rumble is a young inventor with a temper. Using nothing more than his own two hands and a heap of scrap, the feisty yordle constructed a colossal mech suit outfitted with an arsenal of electrified harpoons and incendiary rockets. Though others may scoff...
Rumble.Notes: Rumble's passive (Junkyard Titan) builds Heat from casting abilities — between 50-99% Heat he enters the 'Danger Zone' where his Q (Flamespitter), W (Scrap Shield), and E (Electro Harpoon) all gain significantly stronger effects, but hitting 100% Heat overheats him, silencing his abilities while granting bonus attack speed and on-hit magic damage; Flamespitter is a channeled cone burn that deals damage over time and pushes waves hard, Electro Harpoon is a skillshot slow that stacks magic resist reduction on repeated hits, and his ultimate (The Equalizer) launches a long line of rockets that creates a lingering burning, slowing trail — one of the best zone-control/teamfight ultimates in the game for cutting off an escape route or zoning enemies away from an objective; but managing Heat is a constant balancing act (overheating at the wrong time can silence him out of a kill), and he has zero mobility or escape tools, making him vulnerable to dive compositions and gap-closing duelists once his zone control is bypassed.

Ryze.name: Ryze
Ryze.title: the Rune Mage
Ryze.blurb: Widely considered one of the most adept sorcerers on Runeterra, Ryze is an ancient, hard-bitten archmage with an impossibly heavy burden to bear. Armed with immense arcane power and a boundless constitution, he tirelessly hunts for World Runes—fragments...
Ryze.Notes: Ryze's kit is built around a spell-sequencing combo: his E (Spell Flux) marks a target and spreads to nearby enemies, his W (Rune Prison) roots instead of slowing if the target has Flux, and his Q (Overload) deals bonus bouncing damage against Flux-marked targets while its cooldown is refreshed by casting his other spells, letting him chain an entire combo almost instantly; his ultimate (Realm Warp) opens a channeled portal that, after a delay, teleports himself and all nearby allied units to the target location, becoming a genuine team-wide global repositioning tool for split-pushing, defending objectives, or ambushing a fight from an unexpected angle; his passive (Arcane Mastery) scales his damage off bonus mana and grants him more max mana per Ability Power, making him one of the best-scaling mages in the game with the right itemization, but his root only applies with a Flux-primed combo (otherwise it's just a slow), he has zero personal mobility, and his combo execution has a real skill floor, making him a notoriously weak early laner who needs levels and items to become the dominant late-game threat he's known for.

Samira.name: Samira
Samira.title: the Desert Rose
Samira.blurb: Samira stares death in the eye with unyielding confidence, seeking thrill wherever she goes. After her Shuriman home was destroyed as a child, Samira found her true calling in Noxus, where she built a reputation as a stylish daredevil taking on...
Samira.Notes: Samira's passive (Daredevil Impulse) builds a Style meter from hitting enemies with unique attacks/abilities (never repeating the same one back-to-back), and at max Style ('S' rank) she can unleash her ultimate (Inferno Trigger), a rapid-fire AoE barrage hitting everyone nearby; her passive also lets her execute-style knock up and rapid-strike any immobilized enemy — meaning she thrives specifically off her team's crowd control — her E (Wild Rush) is a dash through a target that resets on a takedown, letting her chain across a whole fight, and her W (Blade Whirl) destroys all incoming enemy projectiles while dealing damage, a strong defensive/outplay tool against poke or burst mages; but she has an extremely short auto-attack range for a marksman, no personal CC of her own, and needs her team (or an immobilized enemy) to unlock her full potential, making her highly reliant on coordinated engage compositions.

Sejuani.name: Sejuani
Sejuani.title: Fury of the North
Sejuani.blurb: Sejuani is the brutal, unforgiving Iceborn warmother of the Winter's Claw, one of the most feared tribes of the Freljord. Her people's survival is a constant, desperate battle against the elements, forcing them to raid Noxians, Demacians, and Avarosans...
Sejuani.Notes: Sejuani's passive (Fury of the North) stacks Frost on enemies hit by her Winter's Wrath or by nearby allied melee autos, and at 4 stacks she can trigger Permafrost, a targeted stun on the Frozen enemy — meaning she stuns far more reliably and often when playing alongside melee-heavy teams; her Q (Arctic Assault) is a knockup dash that doubles as engage, escape, or a channel-interrupt, and her ultimate (Glacial Prison) throws a bola that stuns the first champion hit, traveling further for a bigger stun before shattering into a slowing frost storm — one of the best teamfight-starting ultimates in the game, especially against squishy carries without a Quicksilver Sash; her passive also grants Frost Armor (bonus resistances and slow immunity) when she avoids taking damage, making her hard to punish in the early game, but she relies heavily on teammates to help stack Frost and struggles against ranged kiting compositions that can disengage before she closes the distance.

Senna.name: Senna
Senna.title: the Redeemer
Senna.blurb: Cursed from childhood to be haunted by the supernatural Black Mist, Senna joined a sacred order known as the Sentinels of Light, and fiercely fought back—only to be killed, her soul imprisoned in a lantern by the cruel specter Thresh. But refusing to...
Senna.Notes: Senna's passive (Absolution) harvests Mist Wraiths that spawn from nearby deaths — every unit that dies near Senna may drop a wraith, and each stack grants permanent bonus attack damage, with every 20 stacks adding bonus attack range and critical strike chance,  making her one of a small handful of champions who scale infinitely rather than capping out; her Q (Piercing Darkness) pierces through units, damaging enemies and healing allies in a line, letting her function as marksman and support simultaneously, her W (Last Embrace) roots after a delay if the target doesn't escape the mist, her E (Curse of the Black Mist) camouflages her and nearby allies while granting speed, and her ultimate (Dawning Shadow) is a true global-range beam that shields allies and damages/reveals enemies caught in the center — letting her snipe kills or save allies across the map like Soraka's ultimate.  But she has zero personal mobility, no true escape besides her camouflage, and her root requires a delay that lets alert enemies simply walk out, so she has to rely on positioning, range, and her ultimate's map-wide impact rather than personal combat mobility.

Seraphine.name: Seraphine
Seraphine.title: the Starry-Eyed Songstress
Seraphine.blurb: Born in Piltover to Zaunite parents, Seraphine can hear the souls of others—the world sings to her, and she sings back. Though these sounds overwhelmed her in her youth, she now draws on them for inspiration, turning the chaos into a symphony. She...
Seraphine.Notes: Seraphine's E (Beat Drop) escalates crowd control based on the target's current status — enemies already slowed are rooted instead, and enemies already immobilized or grounded are stunned instead  — making her CC dramatically more reliable alongside teammates who apply slows or roots first; her ultimate (Encore) charms, slows, and reveals every enemy hit, and its range extends every time the projectile strikes an allied or enemy champion,  letting her chain the charm across a whole grouped teamfight if she can thread it through the frontline; her W (Surround Sound) shields nearby allies and, if she's already shielded, heals them as well, and her passive stacks Notes from nearby allies casting spells, empowering her next auto-attack — but she has zero mobility or escape of any kind, and her own CC is comparatively weak in isolation, so she excels specifically when paired with teammates whose slows, immobilizes, or grounding effects let her Beat Drop escalate to its strongest forms.

Sett.name: Sett
Sett.title: the Boss
Sett.blurb: A leader of Ionia's growing criminal underworld, Sett rose to prominence in the wake of the war with Noxus. Though he began as a humble challenger in the fighting pits of Navori, he quickly gained notoriety for his savage strength, and his ability to...
Sett.Notes: Sett's passive (Pit Grit) stores a percentage of damage he takes as Grit, which his W (Haymaker) instantly consumes for a decaying shield before unleashing a true-damage punch in the center of its cone — meaning the more he's hit, the harder he hits back; his E (Facebreaker) pulls enemies in from both his front and back, stunning everyone if it catches at least one target on each side (otherwise it's just a slow/pull), and his ultimate (The Show Stopper) suppresses and carries a single enemy champion across the map before slamming them into the ground, heavily slowing everyone nearby — one of the most impactful engage tools in the game since he can suplex an enemy carry straight into his own team or split the enemy frontline away from their backline.  But he has no dash, blink, or escape of any kind, so ranged kiting champions who can whittle him down and dodge his true-damage combo remain his toughest matchups,  and he falls off in relative impact as the game reaches late-game teamfights against stronger scaling carries.

Shaco.name: Shaco
Shaco.title: the Demon Jester
Shaco.blurb: Crafted long ago as a plaything for a lonely prince, the enchanted marionette Shaco now delights in murder and mayhem. Corrupted by dark magic and the loss of his beloved charge, the once-kind puppet finds pleasure only in the misery of the poor souls...
Shaco.Notes: Shaco's passive (Backstab) empowers his autos, Deceive, and Two-Shiv Poison with bonus damage when striking from behind, and his Q (Deceive) is a short blink that grants brief invisibility, letting him reposition, escape, or set up a backstab crit; his W (Jack in the Box) plants a stealthed trap that fears nearby enemies and attacks them once triggered, giving him strong vision denial and zone control on common paths, and his ultimate (Hallucinate) creates a controllable, semi-independent clone that mimics his abilities and explodes into three mini-boxes fearing and damaging nearby enemies on death — letting his clone distract enemies or force cooldowns during fights.  But he doesn't teamfight like a tank, instead picking off squishies and retreating, and loses impact if the game drags on since most champions get defensive items by then, and he is very fragile without his ultimate up.

Shen.name: Shen
Shen.title: the Eye of Twilight
Shen.blurb: Among the secretive, Ionian warriors known as the Kinkou, Shen serves as their leader, the Eye of Twilight. He longs to remain free from the confusion of emotion, prejudice, and ego, and walks the unseen path of dispassionate judgment between the spirit...
Shen.Notes: Shen's ultimate (Stand United) is the archetypal global teleport — he can channel and warp to any ally anywhere on the map, granting them a large shield, letting him split-push a side lane while still being able to instantly respond to a fight elsewhere  — his E (Shadow Dash) is a skillshot dash that taunts every enemy champion it passes through for 1.5 seconds, making it one of the few multi-target taunts in the game and giving him huge teamfight peel/engage potential,  and his W (Spirit's Refuge) creates a zone around his Spirit Blade that grants 100% dodge chance against basic attacks to all allies standing in it,  making him one of the best answers to auto-attack-reliant champions; his Q (Twilight Assault) recalls the blade to empower his next three autos and slows enemies it passes through. But he has no self-healing and relatively weak damage/waveclear compared to other bruisers, so his value is almost entirely about map-wide pressure, peel, and dodge-tanking rather than winning fights through raw output.

Shyvana.name: Shyvana
Shyvana.title: the Half-Dragon
Shyvana.blurb: Shyvana is a fearsome half-dragon warrior. Though she often appears humanoid, she also rules the skies as a dragon, incinerating her foes with fiery breath. Having saved the life of the crown prince Jarvan IV, Shyvana now serves uneasily in his royal...
Shyvana.Notes: Shyvana's reworked kit (Scalemail) grants stacking armor/magic resist from monster kills, takedowns, and objectives, with dragon kills granting extra stacks and bonus damage; her Fury resource builds passively and from autos, letting her cast her ultimate (Dragon's Descent) once full — this now dashes her to a location in dragon form and fears enemies hit, rather than the old carry/knockback effect,  after which her basic abilities become empowered: Emberstrike (Q) becomes AoE and can be recast twice, Inferno Aegis (W) shields and heals her in dragon form off its delayed detonation, and Molten Burst (E) passes through enemies, marking them and creating slowing zones if it hits multiple targets.  This gives her strong mixed-damage teamfight presence and objective control once transformed, but she lacks hard CC outside her ultimate, which can be unwieldy in effectiveness, so she's prone to being kited by champions who can disengage before or during her dragon form window.

Singed.name: Singed
Singed.title: the Mad Chemist
Singed.blurb: Singed is a brilliant alchemist of dubious morality, whose experiments would turn the stomach of even the most cutthroat criminal. Selling his skills to the highest bidder, he cares little for how his noxious concoctions are used, with the ensuing chaos...
Singed.Notes: Singed's Q (Poison Trail) leaves a damaging trail behind him constantly while active, punishing anyone chasing him through it, and his W (Mega Adhesive) creates a large, extremely potent slow zone on the ground, giving him strong kiting and zone-control tools despite being melee; his E (Fling) picks up a nearby enemy and throws them behind him, which can be used to fling a diving enemy into his own team, throw a squishy carry away from a fight, or reposition an enemy into his poison trail — a uniquely disruptive single-target displacement tool; his ultimate (Insanity Potion) is a pure self-buff granting bonus health, damage, and regeneration with no CC or targeting component, letting him commit hard to extended fights or objective sieges. His playstyle revolves around baiting enemies to chase him through his trail and adhesive rather than trading directly, and champions who can burst him down at range or ignore his kiting entirely (percent-health damage, spell-shields against his fling) tend to give him the most trouble.

Sion.name: Sion
Sion.title: The Undead Juggernaut
Sion.blurb: A war hero from a bygone era, Sion was revered in Noxus for choking the life out of a Demacian king with his bare hands—but, denied oblivion, he was resurrected to serve his empire even in death. His indiscriminate slaughter claimed all who stood in his...
Sion.Notes: Sion's W (Soul Furnace) permanently stacks bonus max health from farming and takedowns, meaning his health pool grows infinitely over the course of the game, and its shield explodes for bonus damage scaling with max health when popped; his Q (Decimating Smash) is a charge-up slam that knocks up and stuns based on charge time, but is not visible to enemies if he isn't visible while charging, making walls and brush an effective way to surprise opponents,  though it still requires good setup to land reliably; his E (Roar of the Slayer) is a short-range fear that's a strong combo-starter for Decimating Smash, and his ultimate (Unstoppable Onslaught) lets him charge in a direction with unstoppable status (immune to all CC and displacement) for as long as he wants, knocking up and stunning the first champion he collides with; his passive (Glory in Death) reanimates him as an unstoppable, movement-speed-boosted zombie for a few seconds after dying, letting him get a final burst of damage or even a revenge kill before actually dying. His biggest weakness is that most of his kit is skillshot-and-setup dependent rather than guaranteed, so ranged kiting champions who can dodge his charge-up Q and avoid his short-range fear give him the most trouble.

Sivir.name: Sivir
Sivir.title: the Battle Mistress
Sivir.blurb: Sivir is a renowned fortune hunter and mercenary captain who plies her trade in the deserts of Shurima. Armed with her legendary jeweled crossblade, she has fought and won countless battles for those who can afford her exorbitant price. Known for her...
Sivir.Notes: Sivir's Q (Boomerang Blade) is a long-range poke/waveclear tool that returns to her, letting her hit enemies twice in one throw, and her W (Ricochet) empowers her next attacks to bounce between up to 8 nearby enemies, giving her arguably the best AoE teamfight and waveclear damage of any marksman; her E (Spell Shield) blocks a single incoming hostile ability entirely and heals/speeds her up on a successful block, making her one of the best answers to key enemy engage or burst spells, and her ultimate (On the Hunt) grants a large movement speed burst to herself and nearby allies, turning her team into an unusually fast, hard-to-escape engage or disengage unit. But she has only 500-unit auto-attack range and no dashes, so Flash is her only hard escape tool outside of her ultimate's speed,  making her vulnerable to poke mages and ranged champions who can punish her short attack range before she closes distance.

Skarner.name: Skarner
Skarner.title: the Primordial Sovereign
Skarner.blurb: The ancient, colossal brackern Skarner is revered in Ixtal as one of the founding members of its ruling caste, the Yun Tal. Devoted to keeping his nation safe from the rest of the world, Skarner dwells in a chamber beneath Ixaocan where he can hear the...
Skarner.Notes: Skarner's kit centers on his passive (Quaking), which stacks from hits with Shattered Earth, Upheaval, and Impale, dealing percent-max-health damage at max stacks; his Q (Shattered Earth) shields him and slams the ground for AoE damage and slow, his E (Upheaval) empowers his next three attacks with bonus range/damage before the third throws a rock that slows on impact (or can be recast as a standalone skillshot), and his ultimate (Impale) is a genuine game-changer: he charges forward ignoring all terrain, and can grab up to three enemy champions within its effective range, suppressing and dragging them with him even over walls for a fixed duration.  This gives him one of the best team-wide pick/engage tools in the game if he catches multiple squishies bunched together, though he can't cast Q, E, or Flash during the ultimate's duration,  leaving him committed once he engages. Note: Riot has publicly discussed a further, more thematic VGU for Skarner still in development as of early 2026, so his kit may change again beyond what's captured here.

Smolder.name: Smolder
Smolder.title: the Fiery Fledgling
Smolder.blurb: Hidden amongst the craggy cliffs of the Noxian frontier, under the watchful eyes of his mother, a young dragon is learning what it means to be heir to the Camavoran imperial dragon lineage. Playful and eager to grow up, Smolder looks for any excuse to...
Smolder.Notes: Smolder's passive (Dragon Practice) grants permanent, uncapped stacks from hitting champions with abilities or killing minions with Q, and his abilities scale directly off these stacks — he's one of a small handful of champions with a truly infinite-scaling stat  — his Q (Super Scorcher Breath) evolves at stack thresholds into an AoE burn and eventually a true-damage execute, his W (Achooo!) is a poke/slow/waveclear tool, and his E (Flap, Flap, Flap) lets him briefly fly, ignore terrain, gain speed, and auto-fire bolts at the lowest-health nearby enemy, giving him one of the safest self-peel tools among ADCs; his ultimate (MMOOOMMMM!) is a slow-moving fire wave that heavily damages and slows enemies in its center while healing him if it connects. But Smolder is at his weakest in the early game  before his stacks accumulate, and his short range makes him vulnerable to hookshot supports like Nautilus, Thresh, Blitzcrank, and Pyke, who can abuse well-placed hooks and Flashes to punish him despite his flight escape.

Sona.name: Sona
Sona.title: Maven of the Strings
Sona.blurb: Sona is Demacia's foremost virtuoso of the stringed etwahl, speaking only through her graceful chords and vibrant arias. This genteel manner has endeared her to the highborn, though others suspect her spellbinding melodies to actually emanate magic—a...
Sona.Notes: Sona's Power Chord passive builds a stack every few basic ability casts, and at max stacks empowers her next auto with bonus damage plus an effect based on whichever ability she last used — Hymn of Valor's Power Chord (Staccato) deals extra damage, Aria of Perseverance's (Diminuendo) reduces the target's damage output, and Song of Celerity's (Tempo) slows the target  — giving her a constant stream of poke, peel, or engage utility depending on which spell she weaves in; her Q/W/E all generate short-lived auras that buff nearby allies with bonus damage, a shield, or movement speed respectively, while her ultimate (Crescendo) fires a traveling soundwave that stuns each enemy hit for the first time and slows enemies caught inside its path,  making it one of the best teamfight-starting or teamfight-saving ultimates among supports. She has no self-mobility outside Song of Celerity's speed buff and no hard escape, so she's very reliant on staying near her team and using her speed aura defensively rather than diving in.

Soraka.name: Soraka
Soraka.title: the Starchild
Soraka.blurb: A wanderer from the celestial dimensions beyond Mount Targon, Soraka gave up her immortality to protect the mortal races from their own more violent instincts. She endeavors to spread the virtues of compassion and mercy to everyone she meets—even...
Soraka.Notes: Soraka's Q (Starcall) is a skillshot zone that damages and slows enemies while healing her if it hits a champion, and her W (Astral Infusion) sacrifices a portion of her own health to heal an ally — the two combine into her core loop of poking for self-sustain, then spending that health to top off a teammate; her E (Equinox) is a two-part zone that silences enemies standing in it and roots anyone still there when it expires, making it a strong disengage/anti-dive tool that can also block off a jungler's gank path, and her ultimate (Wish) is a genuine global heal for herself and all allied champions anywhere on the map, with bonus healing on anyone below 40% health — one of the best clutch team-saving tools in the game. But she has zero self-mobility or escape, and the enemy will often prioritize killing her early in a fight since she has no way to peel for herself and her healing is what keeps her team alive,  making hard-engage divers and assassins her biggest threat.

Swain.name: Swain
Swain.title: the Noxian Grand General
Swain.blurb: Jericho Swain is the visionary ruler of Noxus, an expansionist nation that reveres only strength. Though he was cast down and crippled in the Ionian wars, his left arm severed, he seized control of the empire with ruthless determination… and a new...
Swain.Notes: Swain's passive (Ravenous Flock) collects Soul Fragments from Vision of Empire, Nevermove, and enemy deaths, each stack permanently granting bonus health and instant healing on pickup, giving him infinite scaling similar to Nasus or Cho'Gath; his E (Nevermove) fires a wave that homes back to Swain and roots enemies on its return, and can be recast while they're rooted to pull them toward him and collect a Soul Fragment from each,  forming his core engage tool, while his W (Vision of Empire) is a long-range delayed reveal-and-slow that's much easier to land on an already-rooted or CC'd target; his ultimate (Demonic Ascension) transforms him into a channeling drain-tank that continuously damages and heals off nearby enemies for as long as he wants, and can be ended early with Demonflare, a slowing AoE nova — making him one of the best extended-teamfight anchors in the game once stacked. But high mobility counters all of his basic abilities, since Death's Hand does more damage the closer he is, Vision of Empire has a long delay, and Nevermove needs to travel out and back to matter,  so mobile assassins and dash-heavy duelists who can avoid his setup or burst him down before Demonic Ascension stabilizes him remain his toughest matchups.

Sylas.name: Sylas
Sylas.title: the Unshackled
Sylas.blurb: Raised in one of Demacia's lesser quarters, Sylas of Dregbourne has come to symbolize the darker side of the Great City. As a boy, his ability to root out hidden sorcery caught the attention of the notorious mageseekers, who eventually imprisoned him...
Sylas.Notes: Sylas's ultimate (Hijack) steals the ultimate ability of any champion he's damaged (ally or enemy) and can use it as his own on a shared cooldown, meaning his identity and matchup dynamics shift entirely based on what's available on the enemy team — stealing a Malphite or Amumu ult turns him into a hard-engage tank-diver, while stealing a Karthus or Ashe ult turns him into a global threat; his W (Kingslayer) is a dash-execute that deals bonus damage to low-health targets and heals him, his E (Abscond/Abjure) is a shield-dash that can be recast as a knockback whirlwind, and his passive empowers his next auto after casting a spell — making him a strong extended-fight duelist independent of his ultimate. But his kit outside Hijack is fairly standard assassin fare, so his power level swings heavily based on what ultimates are available to steal in a given game, and champions with no meaningful ultimate to take (or suppression/spell-shields that block his steal) neutralize a major part of his kit.

Syndra.name: Syndra
Syndra.title: the Dark Sovereign
Syndra.blurb: Syndra is a fearsome Ionian mage with incredible power at her command. As a child, she disturbed the village elders with her reckless and wild magic. She was sent away to be taught greater control, but eventually discovered her supposed mentor was...
Syndra.Notes: Syndra's Q (Dark Sphere) spawns a controllable dark sphere at a target location, and her W (Force of Will) picks up a nearby sphere (or minion/monster) and throws it — hitting an enemy champion with a sphere stuns them, making the Q-into-W combo her core setup, though it requires two separate skillshots to land in sequence; her E (Scatter the Weak) knocks back nearby enemies and any spheres, letting her fling a sphere at a target for a delayed stun setup or peel divers off her; her ultimate (Unleashed Power) gathers every available sphere (including any pre-placed ones) and hurls them all at a single target for massive burst damage, making her one of the best single-target burst/execute mages in the game once she's stacked spheres beforehand for a surprise all-in. But her entire combo is skillshot-and-setup dependent with no guaranteed CC, she has zero mobility of her own, and mobile assassins who can close the distance or dodge her spheres punish her hardest.

TahmKench.name: Tahm Kench
TahmKench.title: The River King
TahmKench.blurb: Known by many names throughout history, the demon Tahm Kench travels the waterways of Runeterra, feeding his insatiable appetite with the misery of others. Though he may appear singularly charming and proud, he swaggers through the physical realm like a...
TahmKench.Notes: Tahm Kench's passive (An Acquired Taste) stacks up to 3 times from his empowered on-hit autos and Tongue Lash, and the target is stunned for 1.5 seconds once 3 stacks are consumed by another Tongue Lash,  forming his core setup; his W (Abyssal Dive) is a channel-then-blink that knocks up and stuns nearby enemies on arrival, refunding cooldown and mana if it hits a champion,  giving him both an engage and repositioning tool for himself and any devoured passenger; his ultimate (Devour) swallows a champion — dealing magic damage if they're an enemy, or shielding them if they're an ally  — functioning as an uncleansable single-target suppression when used offensively, or a guaranteed save/peel tool when used on a teammate, making him uniquely flexible between engage and protect playstyles; his E (Thick Skin) stores damage taken as grey health that converts into a shield on activation, giving him excellent sustain in extended trades. But his wave clear is notably weak, and outside Tongue Lash and the new Devour-steal range, his overall range is severely limited,  so ranged poke champions who can whittle him down before he closes distance are his toughest matchups.

Taliyah.name: Taliyah
Taliyah.title: the Stoneweaver
Taliyah.blurb: Taliyah is a nomadic mage from Shurima, torn between teenage wonder and adult responsibility. She has crossed nearly all of Valoran on a journey to learn the true nature of her growing powers, though more recently she has returned to protect her tribe...
Taliyah.Notes: Taliyah's Q (Threaded Volley) leaves Worked Ground behind it, and recasting on that ground consumes it for a single stronger boulder that deals bonus damage and slows,  making positioning central to her damage output; her W (Seismic Shove) knocks a target in a chosen direction after a brief delay with no damage of its own, existing purely to set up her E (Unraveled Earth), a field of stones that stuns enemies that dash through them for the duration of the dash,  making her one of the best anti-mobility mages against dash-reliant matchups when the combo lands; her ultimate (Weaver's Wall) is a genuine map-spanning wall she can ride across the map, letting her block enemies from approaching an objective, seal off escape paths, or rescue herself from a bad spot,  giving her exceptional roaming and split-map control. But she loses much of her potential without wave priority, and compositions that control her wave reduce her map impact to nothing without needing to kill her directly,  and her entire CC chain is a multi-part combo that's easy for aware, mobile opponents to dodge before it fully connects.

Talon.name: Talon
Talon.title: the Blade's Shadow
Talon.blurb: Talon is the knife in the darkness, a merciless killer able to strike without warning and escape before any alarm is raised. He carved out a dangerous reputation on the brutal streets of Noxus, where he was forced to fight, kill, and steal to survive...
Talon.Notes: Talon's passive (Blade's End) wounds enemies hit by his abilities, and attacking a fully-stacked enemy deals a large burst of bleed damage,  making his combo timing central to his burst; his Q (Noxian Diplomacy) is a dash-stab that critically strikes if cast from melee range and refunds cooldown/health on a kill, his W (Rake) throws blades in a cone that return with bonus damage and a slow, and his E (Assassin's Path) lets him vault over terrain, though each specific wall goes on its own lengthy cooldown after use,  giving him unmatched map mobility for roaming between lanes; his ultimate (Shadow Assault) disperses a ring of blades and grants invisibility plus movement speed, converging the blades onto whoever breaks his stealth first — a flexible engage, escape, or execute tool. But he's heavily reliant on Shadow Assault to escape a fight and is significantly more vulnerable without it, and avoiding Rake's return pass avoids a large chunk of his damage, so suppression/hard CC that locks him down before or during his stealth window, or champions who can outrange/dodge his cone-based W, give him the most trouble.

Taric.name: Taric
Taric.title: the Shield of Valoran
Taric.blurb: Taric is the Aspect of the Protector, wielding incredible power as Runeterra's guardian of life, love, and beauty. Shamed by a dereliction of duty and exiled from his homeland Demacia, Taric ascended Mount Targon to find redemption, only to discover a...
Taric.Notes: Taric's passive (Bravado) charges from casting spells, empowering his next auto to deal bonus damage and reduce all his cooldowns; his W (Bastion) links him to an ally, granting them bonus armor and letting Taric cast his other abilities as if standing at the linked ally's location as well as his own, effectively doubling his AoE heal/stun coverage; his E (Dazzle) is a delayed-detonation stun that gives enemies a visible warning before it lands, making it fairly easy to walk out of unless zoned or CC'd first, and his ultimate (Cosmic Radiance) grants a brief window of true invulnerability to himself and all nearby allies after a telegraphed delay, making it one of the best anti-burst, fight-winning defensive tools in the game when timed against a key enemy combo. His entire kit revolves around being physically present near his bonded ally and reacting to incoming damage, so he has no self-mobility or escape, making aggressive dive comps that burst him down before he can react his toughest matchups.

Teemo.name: Teemo
Teemo.title: the Swift Scout
Teemo.blurb: Undeterred by even the most dangerous and threatening of obstacles, Teemo scouts the world with boundless enthusiasm and a cheerful spirit. A yordle with an unwavering sense of morality, he takes pride in following the Bandle Scout's Code, sometimes...
Teemo.Notes: Teemo's passive (Guerrilla Warfare) camouflages him after standing still for a moment, letting his next attack from stealth deal bonus damage and reveal himself — a strong ambush/scouting tool in lane skirmishes; his Q (Blinding Dart) disables the target's basic attacks entirely for its duration, making him one of the hardest counters to auto-attack-reliant duelists, and his E (Toxic Shot) adds a stacking poison DoT to all his autos; his ultimate (Noxious Trap) plants stealthed mushroom traps anywhere on the map with multiple charges, each exploding on trigger to blind, slow, and poison anyone caught nearby, giving him unmatched zone-denial and vision-control potential for jungle paths, chokepoints, and objectives, though placing traps effectively takes time and map awareness rather than direct combat impact. But he's extremely squishy and has zero mobility or escape, so once caught by a diving bruiser or assassin, his blind and traps offer no way to disengage.

Thresh.name: Thresh
Thresh.title: the Chain Warden
Thresh.blurb: Sadistic and cunning, Thresh is an ambitious and restless specter of the Shadow Isles. Once the custodian of countless arcane secrets, he was undone by a power greater than life or death, and now sustains himself by tormenting and breaking others with...
Thresh.Notes: Thresh's passive (Damnation) permanently harvests souls from nearby deaths, each stack granting a small chunk of bonus armor and ability power, giving him uncapped scaling similar to Nasus or Sion; his Q (Death Sentence) is a hook skillshot that pulls the first enemy champion hit toward him (or, if recast quickly, pulls Thresh himself to the target instead), forming his signature pick tool but one that can be dodged like any skillshot; his W (Dark Passage) throws a lantern that any ally can click to dash to Thresh and gain a shield, functioning as both an engage enabler and a clutch escape/save tool; his E (Flay) knocks enemies away in the direction he swings his chain, letting him peel divers off a carry or set up a follow-up combo; and his ultimate (The Box) drops a set of walls around him that slow anyone who breaks through them, with the final wall dealing bonus damage and a stronger slow, making it one of the best zone-denial/escape-cutoff ultimates in the game. But his hook is his primary source of guaranteed CC, and it's a fairly slow, well-telegraphed skillshot that experienced opponents can often dodge, so much of his effectiveness depends on landing it or having a team that punishes a whiffed engage.

Tristana.name: Tristana
Tristana.title: the Yordle Gunner
Tristana.blurb: While many other yordles channel their energy into discovery, invention, or just plain mischief-making, Tristana was always inspired by the adventures of great warriors. She had heard much about Runeterra, its factions, and its wars, and believed her...
Tristana.Notes: Tristana's passive (Draw a Bead) grants bonus attack range that scales with level, letting her outrange most other ADCs late game, and her E (Explosive Charge) plants a bomb on a target that detonates after a few seconds or can be triggered early by auto-attacking, dealing bonus damage scaled by the enemy's missing health — making it a strong execute/finisher tool; her Q (Rapid Fire) grants bonus attack speed and true damage on-hit for a short window, and her W (Rocket Jump) is a leap that knocks back enemies on landing and resets its cooldown on a takedown, letting her chain jumps across a fight, dive backline targets, or peel by jumping away and detonating a bomb behind her. This gives her one of the best self-sufficient engage/disengage kits among ADCs, needing very little external setup to threaten a kill, but she's fairly weak in the early game before she stacks range and items, and long-range poke champions who can punish her before her jump/bomb combo comes online tend to give her the most trouble.

Trundle.name: Trundle
Trundle.title: the Troll King
Trundle.blurb: Trundle is a hulking and devious troll with a particularly vicious streak, and there is nothing he cannot bludgeon into submission—not even the Freljord itself. Fiercely territorial, he chases down anyone foolish enough to enter his domain. Then, his...
Trundle.Notes: Trundle's Q (Chomp) bites his target on his next auto, dealing bonus damage while briefly slowing them and sapping some of their attack damage for himself; his W (Frozen Domain) turns a location into his personal zone, granting bonus attack speed, move speed, and increased healing while standing in it, making him hit much harder and sustain far more inside his own domain; his E (Pillar of Ice) creates impassable terrain that slows nearby enemies and knocks back anyone caught at the very center — a well-placed Pillar can block an enemy's escape route, cut off reinforcements from joining a fight, or even cancel a channeled spell like a recall or an enemy ultimate  — and his ultimate (Subjugate) drains a percentage of a target's health, armor, and magic resist over several seconds, healing Trundle for the amount stolen, making him a strong answer to tanky, high-resistance threats. He offers fantastic 1v1 potential and is traditionally used as a counter to other bruisers and tanks,  but he can be kited once caught outside his Frozen Domain, and stance-based or damage-avoidant champions like Udyr, who can simply shrug off Chomp's slow and never take much damage while grinding him down, give him real trouble.

Tryndamere.name: Tryndamere
Tryndamere.title: the Barbarian King
Tryndamere.blurb: Fueled by unbridled fury and rage, Tryndamere once carved his way through the Freljord, openly challenging the greatest warriors of the north to prepare himself for even darker days ahead. The wrathful barbarian has long sought revenge for the...
Tryndamere.Notes: Tryndamere's passive (Battle Fury) generates Fury from autos and critical strikes, converting it into bonus crit chance, while his Q (Bloodlust) grants bonus AD scaling with his missing health and can consume all his Fury for a large self-heal, giving him both offense and sustain from the same resource; his W (Mocking Shout) reduces nearby enemies' attack damage and slows anyone with their back turned, useful for chasing fleeing targets or checking brush; his E (Spinning Slash) is a dash that can traverse terrain, deals damage to everything it passes through, and has its cooldown reduced by critical strikes,  giving him strong mobility and escape options; and his ultimate (Undying Rage) makes him unable to die for 5 seconds no matter how much damage he takes, and can be activated even while affected by crowd control,  making him one of the best clutch-survival, tower-diving duelists in the game. He thrives in isolating opponents rather than group teamfights, and is one of the strongest 1v1 champions in the game especially late,  but he has no hard CC of his own and struggles if kited by ranged, mobile, or true-damage-heavy champions who can whittle him down before his Fury/crit snowball kicks in.

TwistedFate.name: Twisted Fate
TwistedFate.title: the Card Master
TwistedFate.blurb: Twisted Fate is an infamous cardsharp and swindler who has gambled and charmed his way across much of the known world, earning the enmity and admiration of the rich and foolish alike. He rarely takes things seriously, greeting each day with a mocking...
TwistedFate.Notes: Twisted Fate's W (Pick a Card) cycles through three cards he can lock in, empowering his next auto-attack — Blue restores mana and deals damage, Red slows and deals AoE damage, and Gold stuns the target — giving him a versatile toolkit depending on the situation; his Q (Wild Cards) throws a fan of cards through everything in their path, one of the longest-range non-ultimate poke tools in the game, and his passive (Stacked Deck) grants bonus attack speed plus periodic bonus damage on-hit; his ultimate (Destiny) reveals every enemy champion on the map for several seconds and lets him recast to teleport (Gate) to any location, making him one of the best map-pressure and roaming champions in the game, capable of instantly joining a fight or securing a kill anywhere. But he's fairly squishy with no self-sustain and, besides Gate, has no way to escape, relying entirely on Red Card or Gold Card to keep enemies away from him,  so mobile assassins who can burst him down before he lands his stun or teleports away give him the most trouble.

Twitch.name: Twitch
Twitch.title: the Plague Rat
Twitch.blurb: A Zaunite plague rat by birth, but a connoisseur of filth by passion, Twitch is not afraid to get his paws dirty. Aiming a chem-powered crossbow at the gilded heart of Piltover, he has vowed to show those in the city above just how filthy they really...
Twitch.Notes: Twitch's passive (Deadly Venom) stacks true damage on-hit up to 5 times, and his E (Contaminate) detonates all current stacks on nearby afflicted enemies for bonus damage — enemies at max stacks spread the damage and apply max stacks to nearby targets, turning it into a mini AoE nuke  — his Q (Ambush) grants camouflage and a burst of attack speed on breaking stealth, letting him scout, flank, or ambush from an unexpected angle, and his W (Venom Cask) throws a poison cask that slows and applies extra stacks over time. His ultimate (Spray and Pray) transforms his autos into long-range, line-piercing bolts for several seconds, letting him hit an entire grouped enemy team at once and turning tight corridors into a bloodbath. He struggles in the early game due to his very short base range and weak laning damage, but once he has a few levels and his core items, his late-game damage is incredible,  though hard CC can eliminate him quickly since he has no defensive tools of his own, so positioning and entering fights only after key enemy CC is spent is essential.
