Udyr.name: Udyr
Udyr.title: the Spirit Walker
Udyr.blurb: The most powerful spirit walker alive, Udyr communes with all the spirits of the Freljord, whether by empathically understanding their needs, or by channeling and transforming their ethereal energy into his own primal fighting style. He seeks balance...
Udyr.Notes: Udyr's four abilities are all stances rather than a standard Q-W-E-R kit — Udyr has no traditional ultimate, and each of his 4 basic abilities empowers his next two attacks when activated, with a periodic free recast within a short window to Awaken the stance for an additional, stronger effect. Wilding Claw (Tiger) buffs attack speed and damage, Iron Mantle (Bear/Turtle) grants a shield plus lifesteal and healing when Awakened, Blazing Stampede (Ram) grants movement speed and stuns on his first attack while active, with the Awakened version granting brief crowd-control immunity, and Wingborne Storm (Phoenix) creates a damaging, slowing storm around him that can be sent out to chase a target once Awakened. He lacks a long-range engage tool, but compensates with sustained damage, durability, and reliable crowd control, and boasts one of the healthiest and fastest jungle clears in the game. But despite his stance-swapping toolkit, he has no dash or blink of his own, so ranged kiting champions and mobile junglers who can avoid his stick-and-stun pattern give him the most trouble.

Urgot.name: Urgot
Urgot.title: the Dreadnought
Urgot.blurb: Once a powerful Noxian headsman, Urgot was betrayed by the empire for which he had killed so many. Bound in iron chains, he was forced to learn the true meaning of strength in the Dredge—a prison mine deep beneath Zaun. Emerging in a disaster that...
Urgot.Notes: Urgot's passive (Echoing Flames) fires bonus flame blasts from his legs periodically triggered by autos and Purge, dealing bonus physical and percent-max-health damage; his kit chains together unusually well — Corrosive Charge's slow creates the approach window for Disdain, giving him enough time to close the distance and land the stun,  and his W (Purge) unloads rapid on-hit shots that prioritize whichever champion he's already damaged with another ability, syncing with his passive's flame procs; his E (Disdain) is a shielded charge that flings the first enemy champion hit behind him while stunning them and trampling non-champions in his path; and his ultimate (Fear Beyond Death) impales and slows a target, and if they drop below a health threshold, executes them and terrifies nearby enemies, with the channel itself uninterruptible by any crowd control once the chains latch on.  This gives him one of the best chained CC-into-execute combos among top laners, but his abilities are heavily telegraphed with long startup animations, making his E and ultimate easy to predict and dodge if the opponent knows his patterns,  and ranged kiting duelists who can punish his lack of true mobility give him the most trouble.

Varus.name: Varus
Varus.title: the Arrow of Retribution
Varus.blurb: One of the ancient darkin, Varus was a deadly killer who loved to torment his foes, driving them almost to insanity before delivering the killing arrow. He was imprisoned at the end of the Great Darkin War, but escaped centuries later in the remade...
Varus.Notes: Varus's W (Blighted Quiver) applies stacking Blight to enemies hit by his autos or Q, and his E (Hail of Arrows) detonates that Blight for bonus damage on top of its own slow-and-poke zone, forming his core lane trading pattern; his Q (Piercing Arrow) is a charge-up skillshot that gains range and damage the longer it's held, giving him strong poke and execute potential from a distance; and his ultimate (Chain of Corruption) fires a corrupting bolt that roots the first enemy champion hit, then spreads a chain to nearby enemies to root them as well, making it one of the best AoE teamfight-starting or peel ultimates in the game when it catches a grouped team. But the root only spreads to targets standing close to the initial victim, and the whole ability is a single skillshot that can be dodged entirely, so I marked it low reliability; he has no mobility of his own and no sustain, making him dependent on his team's peel and his own kiting/positioning to survive dives.

Vayne.name: Vayne
Vayne.title: the Night Hunter
Vayne.blurb: Shauna Vayne is a deadly, remorseless Demacian monster hunter, who has dedicated her life to finding and destroying the demon that murdered her family. Armed with a wrist-mounted crossbow and a heart full of vengeance, she is only truly happy when...
Vayne.Notes: Vayne's passive (Silver Bolts) stacks on-hit against a single target, and the third consecutive hit deals bonus true damage scaling with the enemy's max health, making her one of the best pure tank-shredders in the game once she's stacking reliably; her Q (Tumble) is a short dash that also resets her attack timer, giving her strong kiting and repositioning in extended fights; her E (Condemn) knocks the target back and stuns them if they collide with terrain, punishing careless positioning near walls; and her ultimate (Final Hour) grants bonus attack damage, brief invisibility on Tumble casts, and greatly increased movement speed when near enemy champions, making her one of the safest and deadliest late-game snowballing hyper-carries in the game. But she's extremely weak and low-range in the early laning phase, has no self-peel outside her Q's dash and passive stealth windows, and relies heavily on stacking her passive on a single target rather than raw burst, so poke mages and ranged champions who can punish her early or whittle her down before she scales tend to give her the most trouble.

Veigar.name: Veigar
Veigar.title: the Tiny Master of Evil
Veigar.blurb: An enthusiastic master of dark sorcery, Veigar has embraced powers that few mortals dare approach. As a free-spirited inhabitant of Bandle City, he longed to push beyond the limitations of yordle magic, and turned instead to arcane texts that had been...
Veigar.Notes: Veigar's passive (Phenomenal Evil Power) permanently stacks bonus AP from hitting enemy champions with abilities and from champion takedowns, giving him one of only a few genuinely uncapped scaling stats in the game, alongside Nasus, Cho'Gath, and Senna; his E (Event Horizon) creates a ring that stuns enemies who cross its border, making it a strong zoning and engage-punishment tool, though it only stuns units crossing the edge — standing inside it is completely safe;  his W (Dark Matter) is a high-damage delayed skillshot from the sky that can be dodged if the enemy reacts to the warning indicator, and his ultimate (Primordial Burst) is a point-and-click nuke that deals increasingly more damage the lower the target's health, capable of one-shotting squishy carries with enough stacked AP. His signature combo — Event Horizon to stun, Dark Matter, Primordial Burst, then Baleful Strike to finish and gain permanent AP  — makes him one of the most feared burst mages once fed, but he's extremely fragile with no mobility or escape, so mobile assassins who can close the gap and kill him before his combo (or Event Horizon's cooldown) is ready remain his hardest matchups.

Velkoz.name: Vel'Koz
Velkoz.title: the Eye of the Void
Velkoz.blurb: It is unclear if Vel'Koz was the first Void-spawn to emerge on Runeterra, but there has certainly never been another to match his level of cruel, calculating sentience. While his kin devour or defile everything around them, he seeks instead to...
Velkoz.Notes: Vel'Koz's passive (Organic Deconstruction) stacks a debuff on enemies hit by his abilities, and enemies at 3 stacks become Researched, taking true damage from further hits and being marked for extra effects across his kit; his Q (Plasma Fission) is a slowing skillshot that splits in two on recast, his W (Void Rift) is a two-hit delayed-damage zone best landed after a slow or knockup, and his E (Tectonic Disruption) is his only hard CC — a delayed knock-up/stun that also knocks back enemies cast near himself; his ultimate (Life Form Disintegration Ray) is a steerable channeled beam that deals true damage to Researched targets, making it devastating in a set-up teamfight but leaving him extremely exposed during the 2.5-second cast. He has no dash, no innate movement speed steroid, and his ultimate is a long channel, making him one of the most positioning-dependent champions in the mid lane,  so champions who can interrupt his channel or close the distance before his combo lands (via blink, dash-reset, or a point-and-click stun) give him the most trouble.

Vex.name: Vex
Vex.title: the Gloomist
Vex.blurb: In the black heart of the Shadow Isles, a lone yordle trudges through the spectral fog, content in its murky misery. With an endless supply of teen angst and a powerful shadow in tow, Vex lives in her own self-made slice of gloom, far from the revolting...
Vex.Notes: Vex's kit is built around punishing mobility: her passive (Doom) periodically empowers her next basic ability to knock down and fear affected enemies, causing them to flee from her and be slowed based on distance, and its cooldown resets on respawn,  while her innate (Gloom) marks any nearby enemy who dashes or blinks — Vex despises anything that moves fast, and her anti-dash mechanic reflects that,  since her next auto, Q, or W against a marked target consumes the mark for bonus damage and refunds part of Doom's cooldown; her Q (Mistral Bolt) is a piercing wave that accelerates and narrows after traveling, her W (Personal Space) is a self-shield-and-nova, and her E (Looming Darkness) is a large slowing zone that also applies Gloom; her ultimate (Shadow Surge) marks the first enemy champion hit, then lets her dash to them with displacement immunity, and if the target dies within 6 seconds of being marked, Shadow Surge can be cast again at no cost,  giving her genuine reset-chaining potential in extended fights. She thrives against high-mobility champions and works best with junglers/supports who can initiate, creating windows for her fear and resets,  but she has no mobility outside her ultimate's target-locked dash, so champions who can burst her down or apply CC before she reaches Doom/Gloom range remain a threat.

Vi.name: Vi
Vi.title: the Piltover Enforcer
Vi.blurb: Raised on the mean streets of Zaun, Vi is a hotheaded, impulsive, and fearsome woman with very little respect for authority. She has always been a shrewd survivor, both from her youthful troublemaking topside and an unfairly long stint in Stillwater...
Vi.Notes: Vi's passive (Denting Blows) stacks from autos and Vault Breaker, with the third hit dealing bonus max-health damage, shredding armor, and granting attack speed, making her hit progressively harder in an extended trade; her Q (Vault Breaker) is a chargeable dash that knocks back the first enemy champion it collides with, dealing more damage the longer it's charged; her E (Relentless Force) is a piercing cone attack usable twice via stored charges, resetting her combo and applying Denting Blows; and her ultimate (Cease and Desist) is displacement-immune for its entire duration,  letting her charge down a single target through walls and crowd control, knock them into the air, and slam them back down, making it one of the best isolation-pick tools among junglers for deleting a priority target out of a fight. But champions who either displace or kite her effectively cause real issues,  and her all-in combo commits her fully to one target, so tanky or mobile champions who can survive or dodge the initial engage give her the most trouble.

Viego.name: Viego
Viego.title: The Ruined King
Viego.blurb: Once ruler of a long-lost kingdom, Viego perished over a thousand years ago when his attempt to bring his wife back from the dead triggered the magical catastrophe known as the Ruination. Transformed into a powerful, unliving specter tortured by an...
Viego.Notes: Viego's passive (Sovereign's Domination) lets him briefly possess an enemy champion he helps kill, healing for a portion of their max health and temporarily gaining their items, attacks, and non-ultimate abilities, plus a free cast of his own ultimate,  letting him chain kills across an entire teamfight by hopping from body to body — a genuinely unique mechanic that makes his effective kit different every game depending on who he possesses; his W (Spectral Maw) is a chargeable dash-stun where the stun duration and mist range scale with charge time, though the damage and dash distance do not,  and his E (Harrowed Path) creates a mist trail that grants camouflage and bonus speed/attack speed while inside it, though it cannot dash over walls, unlike many other jungler mobility tools;  his ultimate (Heartbreaker) blinks him forward with CC immunity, striking the lowest-health nearby enemy for an execute-style hit and knocking back everyone else caught in the blast. But without possessing someone, he has fairly limited peel or lockdown of his own, and his kit rewards waiting out enemy cooldowns before diving in,  so suppression or hard CC that can lock him down before he secures a possession kill remains his biggest weakness.

Viktor.name: Viktor
Viktor.title: the Herald of the Arcane
Viktor.blurb: The fully biomechanical evolution of his former self, Viktor has embraced his Glorious Evolution and become something of a messiah to his followers. He sacrificed his own humanity under the logic that eliminating emotion would thereby eliminate...
Viktor.Notes: Viktor's passive (Glorious Evolution) permanently upgrades a basic ability every time he collects 100 Hex Fragments from kills/takedowns, and once all three basic abilities are augmented, his ultimate automatically augments too — Q's augment (Turbocharge) grants him bonus shield strength and move speed after casting, W's augment causes his other abilities to slow enemies hit, and E's augment (Aftershock) adds a delayed explosion along the laser's path  — letting his kit visibly grow in power over the course of a game entirely through his own farming and fighting rather than item purchases; his W (Gravity Field) is a zone that slows enemies and stuns anyone who lingers too long inside it, his E (Hextech Ray, formerly Death Ray) is a long-range line poke, and his ultimate (Arcane Storm, formerly Chaos Storm) is a persistent damage cloud that automatically follows champions it has recently damaged, creating constant pressure in teamfights,  and interrupts channeled abilities on cast. He thrives once teams start grouping together and his control of the battlefield increases the closer enemies get to him,  but he has no mobility of his own and needs time to fully evolve his kit, making him vulnerable early and to mobile assassins who can burst him down before his augments come online.

Vladimir.name: Vladimir
Vladimir.title: the Crimson Reaper
Vladimir.blurb: A fiend with a thirst for mortal blood, Vladimir has influenced the affairs of Noxus since the empire's earliest days. In addition to unnaturally extending his life, his mastery of hemomancy allows him to control the minds and bodies of others as easily...
Vladimir.Notes: Vladimir's passive (Crimson Pact) converts a portion of his bonus health into AP and vice versa, meaning any item he buys — tank or damage — boosts both his survivability and his output, and he uses health instead of mana as his resource; his Q (Transfusion) heals him on a point-and-click drain, empowering into a much stronger version every couple of casts; his W (Sanguine Pool) makes him fully untargetable and ghosted for 2 seconds while damaging and slowing enemies standing on the pool, letting him dodge crucial skillshots and access the enemy backline more safely than almost any other mage;  his E (Tides of Blood) is a chargeable nova of blood bolts that costs his own health but slows and deals more damage the longer it's charged; and his ultimate (Hemoplague) marks an area so infected enemies take increased damage from all sources before detonating for a burst of damage and self-healing per champion hit, making it one of the best damage-amplification tools for a coordinated team burst. He's one of the best teamfighters in the game once scaled, capable of carrying games single-handedly, and being able to become untargetable makes him hard to burst down or lock out of a backline dive,  but he has no mobility outside Sanguine Pool's brief speed boost and needs time and items to reach his full power, so hard suppression or displacement-based CC that bypasses his pool's untargetability remains his biggest threat.

Volibear.name: Volibear
Volibear.title: the Relentless Storm
Volibear.blurb: To those who still revere him, the Volibear is the storm made manifest. Destructive, wild, and stubbornly resolute, he existed before mortals walked the Freljord's tundra, and is fiercely protective of the lands that he and his demi-god kin created...
Volibear.Notes: Volibear's passive stacks attack speed from abilities and autos, and at max stacks his attacks chain lightning to nearby enemies, giving him strong extended-fight and waveclear scaling; his Q (Thundering Smash) grants bonus speed while running at a target — if he becomes immobilized before landing the stun, the effect ends early but its cooldown resets, letting him try again quickly  — and lets him pass through units and terrain briefly to reach his target; his W (Frenzied Maul) marks and damages a target, dealing bonus damage and healing him if reused on the same wounded target; his E (Sky Splitter) is a lightning strike that slows enemies and shields him if he's caught in his own blast; and his ultimate (Stormbringer) is a CC-immune leap that slows enemies on landing and disables nearby enemy turrets for several seconds,  also granting him bonus health and size — making him one of the best tower-diving, unstoppable engage tools among top laners/junglers. But the stun from Thundering Smash is his only hard crowd control in the whole kit,  so ranged kiting champions who can avoid it and punish his lack of true escape mobility remain his hardest matchups.

Warwick.name: Warwick
Warwick.title: the Uncaged Wrath of Zaun
Warwick.blurb: Warwick is a monster who hunts the gray alleys of Zaun. Transformed by agonizing experiments, his body is fused with an intricate system of chambers and pumps, machinery filling his veins with alchemical rage. He bursts from the shadows to prey upon...
Warwick.Notes: Warwick's passive (Eternal Hunger) grants bonus magic damage on-hit that heals him whenever he's below half health, and his W (Blood Hunt) senses all low-health enemy champions globally, granting massively increased out-of-combat movement speed toward them — making him one of the best cross-map cleanup/execute threats in the game; his Q (Jaws of the Beast) lunges and can be held to latch onto and follow a target, and his E (Primal Howl) grants damage reduction before unleashing an AoE fear that also slows fleeing enemies, forming a strong engage-into-lockdown combo; his ultimate (Infinite Duress) is a crowd-control-immune leap that suppresses and repeatedly mauls the first enemy champion he collides with, healing him for all damage dealt,  though it's a skillshot leap that stops at the first target struck, giving enemies more counterplay than the old point-and-click version and rewarding proper positioning/frontlining against him.  The combo of chaining his fear directly into his suppress creates an almost unbroken lockdown window on a single target, but if either ability is dodged or interrupted, he loses much of his kill pressure and has to rely on his tankiness and sustain instead.

Xayah.name: Xayah
Xayah.title: the Rebel
Xayah.blurb: Deadly and precise, Xayah is a vastayan revolutionary waging a personal war to save her people. She uses her speed, guile, and razor-sharp feather blades to cut down anyone who stands in her way. Xayah fights alongside her partner and lover, Rakan, to...
Xayah.Notes: Xayah's passive (Clean Cuts) empowers her attacks to pierce and plant Feathers on the ground after casting an ability, and her E (Bladecaller) recalls all planted Feathers back to her, dealing damage to everything they pass through and rooting any target hit by at least three Feathers,  making feather placement and positioning the core of her damage and lockdown; her Q (Double Daggers) is a piercing poke that also plants Feathers, her W (Deadly Plumage) is an attack-speed-and-damage steroid that grants bonus movement speed on hitting a champion (and empowers Rakan too if he's nearby, given their canonical bond), and her ultimate (Featherstorm) makes her untargetable while still able to move, letting her dodge lethal abilities that would kill most other ADCs,  while also planting a fresh line of Feathers for an immediate follow-up root. But her attack range is relatively short for an ADC and she lacks a built-in escape tool outside her ultimate, making positioning and awareness crucial,  so long-range poke champions and mobile assassins who can catch her when Featherstorm is down remain her hardest matchups.

Xerath.name: Xerath
Xerath.title: the Magus Ascendant
Xerath.blurb: Xerath is an Ascended Magus of ancient Shurima, a being of arcane energy writhing in the broken shards of a magical sarcophagus. For millennia, he was trapped beneath the desert sands, but the rise of Shurima freed him from his ancient prison. Driven...
Xerath.Notes: Xerath's kit is built entirely around extreme range and siege-style poke: his Q (Arcanopulse) is one of the longest-range skillshots in the game and can be charged for even more damage, his W (Eye of Destruction) is a delayed AoE zone that damages and slows, and his E (Shocking Orb) is a long-range root skillshot that's difficult to land in isolation but devastating when it does; his ultimate (Rite of the Arcane) roots him in place while he fires three artillery shots from anywhere on the map at long range, making him one of the best siege/objective-control ultimates in the game for sniping kills or forcing enemies off Baron/Dragon from a safe distance. His passive (Mana Surge) empowers his next few autos with bonus damage and mana restoration after landing an ability on a champion. But he has zero mobility of any kind and roots himself in place to use his ultimate, so he's extremely vulnerable to being dove or flanked, and mobile assassins who can close the distance before he can kite or land his root give him the most trouble.

XinZhao.name: Xin Zhao
XinZhao.title: the Seneschal of Demacia
XinZhao.blurb: Xin Zhao is a resolute warrior loyal to the ruling Lightshield dynasty. Once condemned to the fighting pits of Noxus, he survived countless gladiatorial bouts, but after being freed by Demacian forces, he swore his life and allegiance to these brave...
XinZhao.Notes: Xin Zhao's Q (Three Talon Strike) empowers his next three attacks, with the third knocking the target airborne — a reliable, guaranteed-hit CC tool once he's already in melee range; his W (Wind Becomes Lightning) slashes and slows nearby enemies while marking the furthest one hit as Challenged, extending his E's (Audacious Charge) range against that target and setting up bonus effects; and his ultimate (Crescent Guard) deals damage to nearby enemies based on their current health and knocks all of them back except the Challenged target, while granting Xin Zhao damage reduction from anything outside the created circle for several seconds,  making it one of the best isolation/anti-poke tools among junglers — he can dive a priority target, wall off their team's follow-up with the knockback, and shrug off ranged retaliation while dueling them alone. But he relies heavily on completing his Three Talon Strike combo for damage and cooldown resets, so preventing him from finishing it has a dramatic effect,  and tanky junglers with displacement immunity or hard CC that interrupts his combo before it lands give him the most trouble.

Yasuo.name: Yasuo
Yasuo.title: the Unforgiven
Yasuo.blurb: An Ionian of deep resolve, Yasuo is an agile swordsman who wields the air itself against his enemies. As a proud young man, he was falsely accused of murdering his master—unable to prove his innocence, he was forced to slay his own brother in self...
Yasuo.Notes: Yasuo's passive (Way of the Wanderer) grants a periodically-refreshing shield when he's moving and doubles his critical strike damage, encouraging constant mobility; his Q (Steel Tempest) is a three-hit combo whose third cast knocks up any enemy hit — including any airborne target regardless of the count, meaning any ally's knockup instantly enables his own — and his W (Wind Wall) blocks all incoming enemy projectiles for a few seconds, a powerful defensive tool against poke-heavy or projectile-reliant compositions; his E (Sweeping Blade) is a dash through a target that resets its cooldown on hitting an enemy, giving him excellent mobility and chase potential; and his ultimate (Last Breath) knocks up and suspends every airborne enemy near him while dashing him to the furthest one, making him one of the best follow-up engage tools in the game whenever an ally lands a knockup of their own. But he has no self-sustain and relies almost entirely on chaining knockups and dashes to stay alive and deal damage, so suppression, tanky sustain duelists, or champions who can lock him down before he gets his combo going give him the most trouble.

Yone.name: Yone
Yone.title: the Unforgotten
Yone.blurb: In life, he was Yone—half-brother of Yasuo, and renowned student of his village's sword school. But upon his death at the hands of his brother, he found himself hunted by a malevolent entity of the spirit realm, and was forced to slay it with its own...
Yone.Notes: Yone's passive (Way of the Hunter) makes his abilities and every-fourth-attack strike simultaneously in both physical and magic damage, letting him scale off crit while ignoring some resistances effectively; his Q (Mortal Steel) is a forward thrust that knocks up on the third cast (or instantly against an already-airborne target), his W (Spirit Cleave) is a cone slash that shields based on damage dealt, and his E (Soul Unbound) lets him leave his body behind as a spirit form to dash forward with bonus movement speed, then recast to snap back to where his body was — giving him unique two-way repositioning within a single dash window; his ultimate (Fate Sealed) dashes him through every enemy in a line, knocking them all up and dealing bonus damage based on how many champions are hit, making him one of the best AoE knockup-and-dive tools among skirmishers. But like Yasuo, he has to actively chain his knockups and dashes to stay relevant, and his E's recast has a real risk if he overcommits since he's forced back to his original position when it ends, so suppression and hard engage that punishes his all-in commitment give him the most trouble.

Yorick.name: Yorick
Yorick.title: Shepherd of Souls
Yorick.blurb: The last survivor of a long-forgotten religious order, Yorick is both blessed and cursed with power over the dead. Trapped on the Shadow Isles, his only companions are the rotting corpses and shrieking wraiths that he gathers to him. Yorick's monstrous...
Yorick.Notes: Yorick's passive spawns graves near dead enemies, and his Q (Last Rites/Awakening) both empowers his next attack and, with three graves nearby, raises a small army of Mist Walkers to fight alongside him — up to four Mist Walkers can be active at once, dealing on-hit damage scaled with Yorick's stats  — his W (Dark Procession) summons a small enclosed ring of destructible terrain that traps enemies inside while Yorick and allies pass through freely,  making it one of the best solo-lane trapping tools in the game; his E (Mourning Mist) marks a target, slowing them and directing his ghouls to prioritize attacking them; and his ultimate (Eulogy of the Isles) summons the Maiden of the Mist, a powerful AI-controlled companion who raises her own Mist Walkers from nearby deaths and can be set loose to split-push a second lane entirely on her own while Yorick fights or pushes elsewhere,  giving him unmatched dual-lane split-push pressure. But he has no gap-closer of any kind, making Flash close to mandatory,  and mobile, kiting, or true-damage duelists who can dodge his wall and outrun his ghoul army give him the most trouble.

Yunara.name: Yunara
Yunara.title: the Unbroken Faith
Yunara.blurb: Unwavering in her devotion to Ionia, Yunara has spent centuries cloistered away in the spirit realm honing her skills with the Aion Er'na, a legendary Kinkou relic. Despite all she has sacrificed, Yunara's vow to rid the land of disharmony and strife...
Yunara.Notes: Yunara's passive (Vow of the First Lands) makes her critical strikes deal bonus magic damage, giving her a genuine hybrid physical/magic damage profile that's hard to itemize against, while her Q (Cultivation of Spirit) builds Unleash stacks from attacking and, once maxed, unleashes bonus attack speed and magic damage on-hit, with her attacks spreading to deal physical damage to nearby enemies, applying life steal and on-hit effects, and able to critically strike;  her W (Arc of Judgement) is a slowing prayer-bead skillshot that lingers and expands at its endpoint; her E grants a decaying speed boost toward enemies, functioning as her self-peel/kite tool; and her ultimate (Transcend One's Self) puts her in a 15-second Transcendent State where her E becomes a straightforward dash long enough to cross small walls, and her W becomes a beam-style Arc of Ruin with a much shorter cooldown,  making her transform into a far more mobile, aggressive skirmisher-carry for the duration. Riot has explicitly stated she is intended strictly for bot lane and will be tuned to stay there,  and outside her ultimate window she has no true escape, so mobile assassins and divers who can catch her before Transcend is up remain her biggest threat.

Yuumi.name: Yuumi
Yuumi.title: the Magical Cat
Yuumi.blurb: A magical cat from Bandle City, Yuumi was once the familiar of a yordle enchantress, Norra. When her master mysteriously disappeared, Yuumi became the Keeper of Norra's sentient Book of Thresholds, traveling through portals in its pages to search for...
Yuumi.Notes: Yuumi's core mechanic is attaching to an ally champion, becoming untargetable and immune to all damage while riding along with them — her Q (Prowling Projectile) is a skillshot that heals her attached ally and deals bonus damage if it hits an enemy near them, her W (You and Me!) is what lets her attach or, if already attached, dash to a different ally and grant them a shield plus a slow zone on landing, and her E (Zoomies) grants her attached ally bonus attack speed and movement speed passively, or a burst of speed for herself when detached; her ultimate (Final Chapter) is a channeled AoE root-and-damage effect she can move during, making it one of her only real offensive tools. This gives her a uniquely safe playstyle — she takes zero risk from positioning while attached — but it comes at the cost of any independent map presence, personal combat strength, or peel outside her limited kit, so if her attached ally gets caught, dove, or forced to disengage, Yuumi has almost nothing to contribute, and mobile divers who can burst her carry down before she can react remain her biggest weakness.

Zaahen.name: Zaahen
Zaahen.title: The Unsundered
Zaahen.blurb: A fallen god wielding both divine and profane power, Zaahen hunts his fellow Darkin while defying the corruption that threatens to consume him. Once willingly sealed within his glaive to stave off madness, he now walks free, noble in heart and vicious...

Zac.name: Zac
Zac.title: the Secret Weapon
Zac.blurb: Zac is the product of a toxic spill that ran through a chemtech seam and pooled in an isolated cavern deep in Zaun's Sump. Despite such humble origins, Zac has grown from primordial ooze into a thinking being who dwells in the city's pipes, occasionally...
Zac.Notes: Zac's passive (Cell Division) sheds a healing chunk on the ground each time an ability lands, and upon taking fatal damage he splits into four bloblets and enters resurrection, instantly restoring half his max health if any survive,  making him one of the hardest champions to permanently kill in a skirmish; his Q (Stretching Strikes) grabs an enemy, and if his empowered follow-up auto hits a different target, he slams them together for a knockup-stun; his W (Unstable Matter) deals percent-max-health damage in an AoE around him, with cooldown reduced by absorbing chunks; his E (Elastic Slingshot) launches him a long distance to knock up enemies at both the launch and landing zones, letting him gank from unwarded angles by bypassing common ward spots entirely;  and his ultimate (Let's Bounce!) bounces him four times, knocking back and slowing everyone he lands near each time, making it one of the best area-denial/disruption ultimates for a grouped teamfight. But his Q's knockup requires precisely slamming two separate targets together, which is hard to land reliably, and he's fairly weak at level 1, with certain mobile skirmish junglers punishing him hard in early invades.

Zed.name: Zed
Zed.title: the Master of Shadows
Zed.blurb: Utterly ruthless and without mercy, Zed is the leader of the Order of Shadow, an organization he created with the intent of militarizing Ionia's magical and martial traditions to drive out Noxian invaders. During the war, desperation led him to unlock...
Zed.Notes: Zed's passive (Contempt for the Weak) grants bonus true damage against low-health enemies, rewarding him for finishing off targets; his W (Living Shadow) sends out a mimicking clone that duplicates his Q and E casts, and can be recast to swap places with it, giving him excellent repositioning, chase, and escape tools; his E (Shadow Slash) is an AoE slash-and-slow around both himself and any active shadow; his Q (Razor Shuriken) is a piercing line skillshot; and his ultimate (Death Mark) makes him briefly untargetable as he dashes through a marked target, storing a percentage of all damage he and his shadows deal to them over the next few seconds before detonating it all at once — Death Mark also spawns a shadow at his original casting position and can be recast to swap back to it,  giving him flexible engage, burst, and escape all wrapped into one ability. He is extremely reliant on Death Mark to secure kills, even against squishy targets, since it accounts for the majority of his damage,  so suppression, hard CC, or spell-shields that can interrupt or negate his ultimate before it detonates remain his biggest weakness.

Zeri.name: Zeri
Zeri.title: The Spark of Zaun
Zeri.blurb: A headstrong, spirited young woman from Zaun's working-class, Zeri channels her electric magic to charge herself and her custom-crafted gun. Her volatile power mirrors her emotions, its sparks reflecting her lightning-fast approach to life. Deeply...
Zeri.Notes: Zeri's passive (Living Battery) makes her basic attacks skillshot-based bursts of physical damage treated as abilities, with moving and casting building charge toward an empowered, bonus-damage attack; her Q (Burst Fire) is her core damage tool and functions as her auto-attack replacement, meaning attack speed reduces its cooldown and cast time; her W (Ultrashock Laser) fires a slowing pulse that expands into a long-range piercing laser if it hits a wall; her E (Spark Surge) is a dash that vaults or grinds over any terrain she touches, energizing her next Burst Fire casts to pierce through enemies,  giving her exceptional terrain-crossing mobility unlike any other ADC; and her ultimate (Lightning Crash) discharges a nova and enters her into an Overcharged state with stacking bonus attack speed and movement speed, during which Burst Fire becomes a faster chain-lightning triple shot. But she's notably weak in the early game due to her short range and low early damage, and her basic attacks are skillshots that can be dodged or missed entirely,  so long-range poke mages and mobile divers who can punish her before she scales into her crit/attack-speed power spike give her the most trouble.

Ziggs.name: Ziggs
Ziggs.title: the Hexplosives Expert
Ziggs.blurb: With a love of big bombs and short fuses, the yordle Ziggs is an explosive force of nature. As an inventor's assistant in Piltover, he was bored by his predictable life and befriended a mad, blue-haired bomber named Jinx. After a wild night on the town...
Ziggs.Notes: Ziggs's Q (Bouncing Bomb) is his primary poke and waveclear skillshot, while his W (Satchel Charge) is a placed bomb that knocks back nearby enemies and self-launches Ziggs if he's caught in the blast, doubling as an escape tool and a turret-execute against low-health structures; his E (Hexplosive Minefield) scatters a field of proximity mines that slow anything that triggers them, making it the best sustained zone-control tool in the artillery mage class, especially placed at choke points to deny movement for up to 10 seconds;  and his ultimate (Mega Inferno Bomb) can be thrown an enormous distance — covering nearly the entire map from most positions —  to poke, execute, or clear a wave from complete safety. But he doesn't do well in 1v1 situations and dies very fast if caught alone, with minimal mobility to escape once engaged directly,  so mobile assassins and divers who can close the distance before he can Satchel Charge away remain his biggest threat.

Zilean.name: Zilean
Zilean.title: the Chronokeeper
Zilean.blurb: Once a powerful Icathian mage, Zilean became obsessed with the passage of time after witnessing his homeland's destruction by the Void. Unable to spare even a minute to grieve the catastrophic loss, he called upon ancient temporal magic to divine all...
Zilean.Notes: Zilean's Q (Time Bomb) sticks a bomb to a target that explodes for AoE damage and slow after a delay, and his W (Rewind) resets the cooldowns of Time Bomb and Time Warp, letting him double-stack bombs on the same target for burst damage; his E (Time Warp) is one of the strongest single-target speed manipulation tools in the game, granting an ally up to 99% bonus movement speed or applying the same amount as a slow to an enemy, functioning almost like a root at max rank;  and his ultimate (Chronoshift) places a protective rune on an ally that, if they'd otherwise die, puts them in brief stasis before reviving them with a chunk of health — the only resurrection ability on a basic cooldown in the game,  making it one of the best game-swinging safety nets for a fed carry or a risky engage. But he's extremely squishy and entirely skillshot-reliant, missing his bombs makes him significantly less effective, and champions with hard engage or dashes/blinks can lock him down or dodge his combo before he reacts,  so hyper-mobile assassins and hard-engage divers give him the most trouble personally, even as he empowers his own team's divers with Time Warp.

Zoe.name: Zoe
Zoe.title: the Aspect of Twilight
Zoe.blurb: As the embodiment of mischief, imagination, and change, Zoe acts as the cosmic messenger of Targon, heralding major events that reshape worlds. Her mere presence warps the arcane mathematics governing realities, sometimes causing cataclysms without...
Zoe.Notes: Zoe's passive (More Sparkles!) empowers her next auto after casting any spell with bonus magic damage; her Q (Paddle Star!) is a skillshot that pauses at max range and can be recast in any direction, dealing more damage the farther it travels; her W (Spell Thief) lets her pick up dropped summoner spells or item actives from nearby deaths or enemy casts and use them once, gaining bonus speed and orbiting homing missiles whenever she casts a spell; her E (Sleepy Trouble Bubble) is her signature CC — it bursts on the first enemy hit, briefly applies drowsy, then puts the target to sleep, during which any damage source wakes them but deals bonus true damage,  and its range extends significantly when fired over terrain,  letting her land surprise picks from unexpected angles; and her ultimate (Portal Jump) blinks her to a location for one second before automatically returning, letting her extend Paddle Star's range, scout over walls, or briefly reposition without a true escape. She has no built-in mobility outside her ultimate, which doesn't offer a full escape since she's pulled back to her original position,  making her heavily reliant on landing her sleep and burst combo before enemies close the distance, and tanky sustain champions or dashers who can punish her commitment give her the most trouble.

Zyra.name: Zyra
Zyra.title: Rise of the Thorns
Zyra.blurb: Born in an ancient, sorcerous catastrophe, Zyra is the wrath of nature given form—an alluring hybrid of plant and human, kindling new life with every step. She views the many mortals of Valoran as little more than prey for her seeded progeny, and thinks...
Zyra.Notes: Zyra's passive (Garden of Thorns) periodically drops seeds around her, and casting Q (Deadly Spines) or E (Grasping Roots) near a seed transforms it into a fighting plant — Deadly Spines spawns a ranged Thorn Spitter, while Grasping Roots spawns a melee, slowing Vine Lasher — giving her a small on-demand army; her W (Rampant Growth) plants seeds manually and grants vision if an enemy steps on one; her E is her primary hard CC, a narrow root skillshot that's notoriously easy to dodge if not respected like a hook; and her ultimate (Stranglethorns) creates a large zone that damages enemies as it expands, then knocks up anyone still inside after a delay, while also empowering any of her plants caught within it to attack twice per hit with bonus health and damage.  Her whole kit is built around chaining Root into Rampant Growth into Stranglethorns to maximize plant uptime and CC, but her ultimate can be evaded at the edges since there's a delay before the knockup triggers, and she has no mobility or escape of her own,  making her extremely vulnerable to being caught out or dove before her plants and root can set up.
